American R&B, pop and jazz singer Patti Austin who had the 1983 US No.1 & UK No.11 single with James Ingram 'Baby Come To Me'. She and Michael Jackson performed a duet on It's the Falling in Love, which appeared on his album Off the Wall,
English musician Peter Beckett, best known as the lead singer and guitarist for 1970s soft rock group Player, which scored a US No. 1 hit in 1977 with 'Baby Come Back'.

American singer Ronnie Spector, who co-founded and fronted the girl group The Ronettes who had the 1963 US No.2 & UK No.4 single 'Be My Baby'. She married producer Phil Spector in 1968. Ronnie alleged in her 1990 memoir, Be My Baby, that following their marriage, Phil subjected her to years of psychological torment and sabotaged her career. Ronnie died on January 12, 2022, aged 78.
Mick Clarke, from English pop band The Rubettes who had the 1974 UK No.1 single 'Sugar Baby Love'.

American singer, guitarist and songwriter, James Griffin who with Bread had the 1970 US No.1 & UK No.5 single 'Make It With You'. He won an Academy Award for Best Original Song in 1970 as co-writer of 'For All We Know'. He died of complications from cancer on 11 January 2005.

American singer and entertainer Eddie Fisher, singer, who had the 1953 UK No.1 single 'Outside Of Heaven', and 1955 US No.6 single 'Heart'. Fisher divorced his first wife, actress Debbie Reynolds, to marry Reynolds' best friend, actress Elizabeth Taylor.
Jimmy Dean, singer, (1961 US No.1 & UK No.2 single 'Big Bad John'. Went on to present a prime time variety show on US TV.

American guitarist and session musician Bill Pitman died at his home aged 102, from complications of a fall. He played ukulele in the Academy Award-winning song 'Raindrops Keep Fallin' on My Head,' and as a session musician played on The Byrds hit 'Mr. Tambourine Man', 'Good Vibrations', The Beach Boys, 'Strangers in the Night', Frank Sinatra, 'Be My Baby', The Ronettes, 'Deep Purple' Nino Tempo & April Stevens and 'These Boots Are Made for Walkin'' Nancy Sinatra.

Scottish singer-songwriter and actor Darius Danesh was found unresponsive in his apartment in Rochester, Minnesota, and he was pronounced dead later that day. He came to prominence after appearing in the first series of UK TV's Popstars contestant in 2001, famous for his rendition of Britney Spears 'Baby One More Time'. Darius scored the 2002 UK No.1 single 'Colourblind' and later performed the role of Billy Flynn in London's West End production of Chicago and played the lead role of Sky Masterson in Guys and Dolls.

American singer and guitarist Trini Lopez died age 83 from complications from COVID-19 amidst the COVID-19 pandemic in California. He scored the 1963 US No.3 & UK No.4 single 'If I Had A Hammer' and the hits 'Lemon Tree', 'I'm Comin' Home, Cindy' and 'Sally Was a Good Old Girl'. He designed two guitars for the Gibson Guitar Corporation: the Trini Lopez Standard, a rock and roll model based on the Gibson ES-335 semi-hollow body, and the Lopez Deluxe, a variation of a Gibson jazz guitar designed by Barney Kessel. Both of these guitars were in production from 1964 until 1971, and are now highly sought-after among collectors. Owners of the guitar include Dave Grohl of Foo Fighters and Noel Gallagher of Oasis.

Ray Parker JR. started a three week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with the theme from the film 'Ghostbusters'. Parker who had been a session guitarist for Stevie Wonder and Marvin Gaye was accused of plagiarizing the melody from Huey Lewis and the News song 'I Want a New Drug', resulting in Lewis suing Parker, the pair settled out of court in 1985.

The Beatles started recording their fourth album ('Beatles For Sale', not yet titled), at EMI studios in London, England. The album marked a departure from the upbeat tone that had characterised the Beatles' previous work, partly due to the band's exhaustion after a series of tours that had established them as a worldwide phenomenon in 1964. Beatles for Sale was not widely available in the US until 1987, when the Beatles' catalogue was standardised for release on CD.

Elvis Presley's double-sided hit 'Don't Be Cruel / Hound Dog' was released. 'Don't Be Cruel' was the first song that Elvis Presley's song publishers, Hill & Range, brought to him to record. Written by Otis Blackwell, who was more than happy to give up 50% of the royalties and a co-writing credit to Presley to ensure that the "hottest new singer around covered it". But unfortunately, he had already sold the song for only $25 ($289 in 2024), as he stated in an interview with American Songwriter. The single went to No.1 on the US chart, where it stayed for 11 weeks - a record that would not be broken until 1992's Boyz II Men hit 'End of the Road'.

Chris Kelly, Kris Kross, (1992 US No.1 & UK No.2 single 'Jump'. The duo of Chris Smith and Chris Kelly were 12 and 13 when they recorded the song. Kelly died on 1st May 2013 in an Atlanta hospital at the age of 34.

works.title: Narrow Stairs
works.artist: Death Cab for Cutie who had the

description: American singer, songwriter and guitarist Ben Gibbard best known as the lead vocalist and guitarist of the indie rock band Death Cab for Cutie who had the 2008 US No.1 album Narrow Stairs. The group took the band name from the song "Death Cab for Cutie", by Bonzo Dog Doo-Dah Band. The song is a track on the Bonzo's 1967 debut album, Gorilla, and was performed by them in The Beatles film Magical Mystery Tour.
Andy Bell, guitarist, singer with Ride who had the 1992 UK No.9 single 'Leave Them All Behind'. Also a member of Hurricane No.1. Bell joined Oasis in 1999.
Hamish Seelochan from English R&B/pop group, The Pasadenas, who had the 1992 UK No.4 single 'I'm Doing Fine Now'.
Paul Gendler guitarist from British pop music band Modern Romance, who had the 1982 UK No.4 single 'Best Years Of Our Lives'.
Joe Jackson, UK singer, songwriter, who had the 1980 UK No.5 single 'It's Different For Girls' and 1982 US No.6 and UK No.7 single 'Steppin Out'.

Erik Braunn, guitarist from American rock band Iron Butterfly who had the 1968 US No.14 single 'In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida'. The band's seminal 1968 album In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida is among the world's 40 best-selling albums, selling more than 30 million copies. He died on 25th July 2003 aged 52.

Eric Carmen, American singer, songwriter, guitarist and keyboardist, who with The Raspberries had the 1972 US No.5 single 'Go All The Way' and the 1976 solo US No.2 single, 'All By Myself', plus other hits with 'She Did It', 'Hungry Eyes', and 'Make Me Lose Control. He died on 11 March 2024 age 74.
Bill Hurd, from English pop band The Rubettes who had the 1974 UK No.1 single 'Sugar Baby Love'.
Jim Kale bassist from Canadian rock band Guess Who who had the 1970 US No.1 & UK No.19 single 'American Woman'.

Denis Payton, sax, from English pop rock band, Dave Clark Five, who scored the 1964 UK No.1 single 'Glad All Over', and the 1965 US No.1 single 'Over And Over' , plus over 15 other UK top 40 singles. Payton died on 17th December 2006.
Mike Hugg, drummer and founding member of the 1960s group Manfred Man who had the 1964 UK & US No.1 single 'Do Wah Diddy Diddy'. He was later a member of Manfred Mann Chapter Three.

works.title: You've Got A Habit Of Leaving

description: American record producer, songwriter, and arranger Shel Talmy. He arranged and produced hits such as 'You Really Got Me' by The Kinks, (and many more hits with the group up to 19670, 'My Generation' by The Who, and 'Friday on My Mind' by the Easybeats. Talmy produced two singles in 1965 by two groups featuring David Bowie, 'I Pity The Fool' by The Manish Boys and 'You've Got A Habit Of Leaving', where the singer was accompanied by The Lower Third. Talmy died from complications of a stroke on 13 November 2024, at the age of 87.

Guitarist Les Paul died in hospital in White Plains, New York at the age of 94 suffering from severe pneumonia. Paul is credited with developing one of the first solid-body electric guitars, which went on sale in 1952 and contributed to the birth of rock. He also developed other influential recording innovations such as multi-track recording and overdubbing. In the early 50s, Paul and his wife Mary Ford had a string of hits including 'Mockin' Bird Hill', 'How High the Moon', and 'Vaya Con Dios'.

UK singer-songwriter Kate Nash went to No.1 on the UK album chart with her debut album Made Of Bricks. The album featured the UK No.2 single, 'Foundations', which spent five weeks at No. 2, being held off by Rihanna and Jay-Z's 'Umbrella'.

Founding member of Destiny's Child, LeToya was No.1 on the US album chart with her debut solo album 'LeToya.' It was released six years after being dismissed from the group and staying away from the spotlight.

In Buffalo, New York, Radiohead started a run of 13 shows opening for Alanis Morissette. They use their time to road-test new songs like 'No Surprises' and 'Paranoid Android,' which appeared on their next album, OK Computer.

Kyu Sakamoto was killed in a plane crash when JAL Flight 123, a 747, crashed and burned on a thickly wooded mountain about 60 miles northwest of Tokyo. He was 43. He had the 1963 US No.1 & UK No.6 single 'Sukiyaki', the first Japanese artist to hit the top of the US singles chart.

works.title: Once, Twice, Three Times a Lady

description: The Commodores started a two week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Three Times A Lady', also No.1 in the UK and becoming Motown's biggest British selling single. Lionel Richie wrote the song about his love for his wife, mother and grandmother hence 'Once, Twice, Three Times a Lady.'

Jimmy Page, Robert Plant, John Paul Jones and John Bonham played together for the first time when they rehearsed at a studio in Gerrard Street in London's West End. The first song they played was a version of 'The Train Kept A-Rollin.' They also played 'Smokestack Lightning' and a version of 'I'm Confused' (soon to become 'Dazed And Confused'). The first live dates they played were as The Yardbirds, and it was not until the following month when they started to use the name Led Zeppelin.

British pop/folk singer-songwriter Tanita Tikaram. Her debut album, Ancient Heart, produced by Rod Argent and Peter Van Hooke, was released in 1988 when she was 19 years old. The album's first two singles, 'Good Tradition' and 'Twist In My Sobriety', became top 10 hits around Europe and the album sold around 4 million copies worldwide.

Paul Tucker, keyboards with English group Lighthouse Family who had the 1996 UK No.4 single 'Lifted' plus 9 other UK Top 40 singles. Their 1995 debut album Ocean Drive sold more than 1.8 million copies in the UK alone.
Sir Mix-A-Lot, American rapper, songwriter, and record producer who had the 1992 US No.1 single 'Baby Got Back'.

Bragi Olaffson, bass from Icelandic alternative rock band The Sugarcubes. Their debut album, Life's Too Good (1988), was an unexpected international success, and produced their signature song 'Birthday'. It is credited as the first Icelandic album to have a worldwide impact and influence Icelandic popular music.
Roy Hay guitar, vocals from English group Culture Club who had the 1983 UK No.1 & 1984 US No.1 single 'Karma Chameleon' plus seven other UK top 10 singles'.
Jurgen Dehmel, from German group Nena who had the 1984 UK No.1 & US No.2 single '99 Red Balloons'. The track made them UK One Hit Wonder.

Australian musician Jerry Speiser, best known as the drummer and a founding member of Men At Work who had the 1983 UK & US No.1 single 'Down Under'. He left the band in 1984 and was a member of other groups including FX, One World and Frost

works.title: Annie I'm Not Your Daddy
works.artist: and subsequently formed and led Kid Creole

description: American musician, singer and songwriter August Darnell. He co-founded Dr. Buzzard's Original Savannah Band and subsequently formed and led Kid Creole and the Coconuts who had the 1982 UK No.2 single 'Annie I'm Not Your Daddy'.

works.title: This Town Ain't Big Enough For The Both Of Us
The Number One Song in Heaven

description: Ronald David Mael from Sparks. The American pop and rock duo had the 1974 UK No.2 single 'This Town Ain't Big Enough For The Both Of Us' and the disco hit 'The Number One Song in Heaven' in 1979, resulting from a collaboration with Giorgio Moroder.

Mark Knopfler British songwriter, guitarist, singer with Dire Straits who had the 1985 US No.1 single 'Money For Nothing', the 1986 UK No.2 single 'Walk Of Life', and the 1985 world-wide No.1 album Brothers In Arms. Knopfler has recorded and performed with many prominent musicians, including Chet Atkins, Eric Clapton, Bob Dylan, Bryan Ferry, Emmylou Harris, Van Morrison, Steely Dan, Sting, and James Taylor.
English pop singer Craig Douglas, who had the 1959 UK No.1 single whith his version of the Sam Cooke hit 'Only Sixteen 'plus nine other UK Top 40 hits.

works.title: Please Send Me Someone to Love

description: American rhythm and blues singer Percy Mayfield, known for the songs 'Please Send Me Someone to Love' and 'Hit the Road Jack', the latter being a song popularized by Ray Charles, (Charles recorded at least 15 of his songs). He died on 11 August 1984 age 63.

works.title: The Breakup Song (They Don't Write
works.artist: and wrote several popular horror novels

description: American rock musician, radio personality, and novelist Greg Kihn died from complications of Alzheimer's disease in the San Francisco Bay Area at the age of 75. He founded and led the Greg Kihn Band and wrote several popular horror novels. He is best known for the hits 'The Breakup Song (They Don't Write 'Em)', US No.15 in 1981 and 'Jeopardy' in 1983.

US singer-songwriter Nanci Griffith died at the age of 68. In 1994 she won a Grammy Award for the album Other Voices, Other Rooms as well as recording duets with many artists, among them Emmylou Harris, John Prine, Don McLean, Jimmy Buffett, Adam Duritz (singer of Counting Crows), Darius Rucker (lead singer of Hootie & the Blowfish) and Willie Nelson.

'Angels' by Robbie Williams was voted the best single which should have been a No.1 but never was, in a poll for VH1. The ballad, which reached No.4 in December 1997, beat Savage Garden's ‘Truly, Madly, Deeply’ and Aerosmith's 'I Don't Want To Miss A Thing.' Other songs said to have deserved a No.1 included Madonna with ‘Ray of Light’, ‘Beautiful Stranger’, ‘Crazy For You’ and ‘Material Girl’, Bon Jovi with ‘Always’ and Oasis with ‘Wonderwall’ and ‘Live Forever’. Sir Cliff Richard's hit 'Millennium Prayer' was voted the worst No.1 single of all time.

Curtis Mayfield was paralyzed from the neck down after lighting equipment fell on him while he was being introduced at an outdoor concert at Wingate Field in Flatbush, Brooklyn, New York. Despite this, he continued his career as a recording artist, releasing his final album New World Order in 1996. He remained a quadriplegic for the next nine years until his death in 1999.

works.title: Give It Up
works.artist: were at No.1 on the UK singles chart

description: KC and the Sunshine Band were at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Give It Up'. The American disco group's only UK chart topper spent three weeks at No.1

American soul singer Joe Tex died at his home in Navasota, Texas, following a heart attack, just five days after his 49th birthday. Had nine US Top 40 hits including the 1972 US No.2 single 'I Gotcha'.

Four masked robbers broke in to Todd Rundgren's New York house and proceeded to steal Hi-Fi equipment and paintings after tying the musician up. It was reported that one of the intruders had been humming his hit 'I Saw The Light'.

Lovin Spoonful started a three week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Summer In The City', it made No.8 in the UK. The song features a series of car horns during the instrumental bridge, starting with a Volkswagen Beetle horn, and ends up with a jackhammer sound, in order to give the impression of the sounds of the summer in the city.

Manfred Mann were at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Do Wah Diddy Diddy', the bands first of three UK No.1's. The song which was written by Jeff Barry and Ellie Greenwich was originally recorded in 1963 by the American vocal group The Exciters.

The original version of 'Hound Dog' was recorded by Willie Mae (Big Mama) Thornton. It would become the first hit for the song-writing team of Jerry Leiber and Mike Stoller and went on to top the Billboard R&B chart for seven weeks, selling nearly two million copies.
Diamond Blue Smith, singer, from American R&B/hip hop group Pretty Ricky who scored the 2007 US No.1 album Late Night Special.

James Morrison, UK singer-songwriter. He rose to recognition for his 2006 debut single 'You Give Me Something', which peaked within the top five on the UK Singles Chart, and scored the 2006 UK No.1 album Undiscovered. At the 2007 Brit Awards, Morrison won the Brit Award for Best British Male from three total nominations, namely British Breakthrough Act and Song of the Year
Mark Nevin, singer, songwriter, from British folk and soft rock band, Fairground Attraction who had the 1988 UK No.1 single 'Perfect'.

Michael Bradley, bassist with the Northern Irish pop punk band The Undertones, who had the 1980 UK No.9 single 'My Perfect Cousin' and the hit singles 'Jimmy Jimmy', 'Here Comes the Summer' and 'You've Got My Number (Why Don't You Use It?)'.
American radio/television personality, comedian Danny Bonaduce who with The Partridge Family had the 1970 US No.1 single 'I Think I Love You', and the 1972 UK No.3 single 'Breaking Up Is Hard To Do'.

Singer, and environmentalist Feargal Sharkey. From Derry, Northern Ireland, he was the lead vocalist of the punk band the Undertones in the 1970s and 1980s, who scored the UK hits 'Teenage Kicks', 'Here Comes The Summer', 'My Perfect Cousin' and 'Wednesday Week'. He became a solo artist in the 1980s and 1990s; his 1985 solo single 'A Good Heart' (written by Maria McKee) was a No.1 hit in the UK. Sharkey is also a lifelong fly fisherman and has campaigned against the pollution of British rivers.

Dan Fogelberg, US singer-songwriter, known for his 1970s and 1980s soft rock hits, including 'Longer' (1979), 'Same Old Lang Syne' (1981), and 'Leader of the Band' (1982). He also worked with Joe Walsh, Jackson Browne, Randy Newman. Fogelberg died on 16th Dec 2007 at his home in Maine at the age of 56 of prostate cancer.
Cliff Fish, bass, from Paper Lace who scored the 1974 UK No.1 single 'Billy Don't Be A Hero', and the 1974 US No.1 single 'The Night Chicago Died'. He died 14 April 2023.
Irish singer and guitarist John Stokes, with The Bachelors, who had the 1964 UK No.1 single 'Diane', plus 16 other UK Top 40 singles.

American pianist, singer, and songwriter Jimmy McCracklin. His style contained West Coast blues, Jump blues, and R&B. Over a career that spanned seven decades he recorded over 30 albums. He had the 1958 No.7 hit 'The Walk' in the US. He died on 20 December 2012, after a long illness, aged 91.

British jazz pianist Sir George Shearing OBE. Shearing who was born blind started to learn piano at the age of three. He was the composer of over 300 songs, including the jazz standards 'Lullaby of Birdland' and 'Conception' and had multiple albums on the Billboard charts during the 1950s, 1960s, 1980s and 1990s. He died of heart failure on 14 February 2011 age 91.

James Blunt topped both the UK singles chart (with 'You're Beautiful'), and album charts ('Back to Bedlam'), for a fifth week in a row, a feat last achieved by Celine Dion. Her single ‘Think Twice’ and album ‘Colour Of My Love’ topped both charts simultaneously for five weeks in 1995.

works.title: Like We Never Loved at All

description: Faith Hill was at No.1 on the US chart with Fireflies, her third consecutive album to debut at No. 1 on both the Country and Billboard album charts. The track 'Like We Never Loved at All' (with Hill's husband Tim McGraw), featured on the album, won the Grammy for Best Country Collaboration at the 48th Grammy Awards in 2006, while 'Mississippi Girl' and Fireflies were nominated for Best Female Country Vocal Performance and Best Country Album.

works.title: When You Say Nothing At All

description: Ronan Keating had the UK No.1 single with 'When You Say Nothing At All'. The debut solo single from the Boyzone lead singer. The song was from the film Notting Hill.

Freddie Mercury had his first solo UK No.1 single with 'Living On My Own'. The song had been a minor hit in 1985 when released from his solo album Mr Bad Guy, this was remixed by Belgian producers No More Brothers and re-released to widespread chart success. The song's lyrics reflect Mercury's longstanding admiration for Greta Garbo, whose quotations are featured prominently in the lyrics.

Tony Williams lead singer with The Platters died in his sleep of emphysema aged 64. He sang most of the group's hits up until 1961 when he was replaced by Sonny Turner. Had the 1959 UK & US No.1 single 'Smoke Gets In Your Eyes'.

Guitarist Roy Buchanan died after hanging himself with his own shirt in Fairfax County Adult Detention Center having been arrested for drunkenness. Buchanan released over 15 solo albums; Jeff Beck dedicated the song 'Cause We've Ended As Lovers' to Buchanan in 1975 on his Blow by Blow album.

Lead singer, poet and frontman of Hawkwind Robert Calvert died of a heart attack. He was a member of Hawkwind from 1972-1979 during which time he co-wrote their hit single 'Silver Machine' and directed their Space Ritual Tour.

The Police released their third single 'Can't Stand Losing You' as the follow-up single to 'Roxanne' which when released the following year peaked at No.2 on the UK chart. Written by singer and bassist Sting as a song about suicide, the song gained minor controversy for its single cover art, featuring Stewart Copeland hanging himself.

The Who released their fifth studio album Who’s Next which featured the classic song 'Won't Get Fooled Again' and has since been viewed by critics as the Who's best record and one of the greatest rock albums of all time. The cover artwork shows a photo of the band apparently having just urinated on a large concrete piling, but according to photographer Ethan Russell, most of the band members were unable to urinate, so rainwater was tipped from an empty film canister to achieve the desired effect. Featuring songs that were initially intended for Lifehouse, an unreleased rock opera and follow-up to the band’s 1969 album, Tommy, the LP has appeared on countless "Best Of" lists over the decades. The album was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame in 2007.

Sonny & Cher started a three-week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'I Got You Babe'. Sonny Bono is said to have been inspired to write the song to capitalise on the popularity of the term "babe," as heard in Bob Dylan's 'It Ain't Me Babe'.

The Beatles taped an appearance for CBS-TV's The Ed Sullivan Show at Studio 50, New York City. They performed ‘I Feel Fine’, ‘I'm Down’, ‘Act Naturally’, ‘Ticket to Ride’, 'Yesterday' and ‘Help!’ Also today, The Beatles fifth album Help! started a nine-week run at No.1 on the UK charts.

US singer Johnny Burnette was killed in a boating accident on Clear Lake California, aged 30. His unlit boat was struck by an unaware cabin cruiser, the impact threw him off the boat and he drowned. Burnette scored the 1961 US No.8 & UK No.3 single 'You're Sixteen'.

American rapper, singer, songwriter and actress Doechii. Doechii's second mixtape, Alligator Bites Never Heal (2024), peaked within the top ten of the Billboard 200. It won Best Rap Album at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards. She also appeared on Tyler, the Creator's song 'Balloon' in 2024, the remix of the Weeknd and Playboi Carti's single 'Timeless' in 2025, and Lady Gaga's song 'Runway' in 2026.
Kevin Cadogan, Third Eye Blind, who had the 1997 US No.4 & UK No. 33 single 'Semi-Charmed Life'.

Mark Collins guitarist with English indie rock band The Charlatans who had the 1990 UK No.9 single 'The Only One I Know'. In the UK, all of the band's thirteen studio albums have charted in the Top 40 of the UK Albums Chart, three of them being No.1s.

works.title: I Lost My Heart To A Starship Trooper

description: English classical crossover soprano singer and actress Sarah Brightman. She had the 1978 UK No. 6 single 'I Lost My Heart To A Starship Trooper' with Hot Gossip. Brightman's 1996 duet with the Italian tenor Andrea Bocelli, 'Time to Say Goodbye', topped the charts all over Europe and became the highest and fastest-selling single of all time in Germany, where it stayed at the top of the charts for 14 consecutive weeks and sold over three million copies.
Sharon Bryant from American band Atlantic Starr who had the 1987 US No.1 & UK No.3 single 'Always'.

Slim Dunlap, from American rock band The Replacements, who released the 1984 album Let It Be. Initially a punk rock band, they are considered pioneers of alternative rock. Dunlap died at his home in Minneapolis on December 18, 2024, at the age of 73.
Maddy Prior, singer with English folk rock band Steeleye Span who formed in 1969. They had the 1975 UK No.5 single 'All Around My Hat' and a hit with 'Gaudete'.
George Newsome from British blues rock group Climax Blues Band, who had the 1977 US No.3 & 1976 UK No.10 single 'Couldn't Get It Right'.

Larry Graham, bass guitar, Sly and The Family Stone, who had the 1968 US No.1 singles 'Everyday People', the 1971 US No.1 'Family Affair' and the 1971 US No.1 album There's a Riot Goin' On. He later formed Graham Central Station.
Ben Sidran, American jazz and rock keyboardist, producer, label owner, and music writer. Early in his career he was a member of the Steve Miller Band that had the 1974 US No.1 single 'The Joker'.

works.title: Juliet
works.artist: The Four Pennies who had the

description: Lionel Morton, singer, guitarist from English 1960s pop group The Four Pennies who had the 1964 UK No.1 single 'Juliet'.

American singer-songwriter and guitarist David Crosby, a founding member of both the Byrds and Crosby, Stills & Nash. With CS&N he had the 1969 UK No.17 single 'Marrakesh Express', and the 1970 US No.1 album Deja Vu. Crosby released eight solo albums over the course of his career. His solo debut was 1971's If I Could Only Remember My Name. Crosby's combined work with the Byrds and CSNY has sold over 35 million albums. He was known for his outspoken personality, politics, and personal troubles: he was sometimes depicted as emblematic of the counterculture of the 1960s. Crosby died on 18 January 2023 age 81.

American country music singer and songwriter Connie Smith. Her debut single 'Once a Day' was nominated at the Grammy Awards for Best Female Country Vocal Performance and reached No.1 on the Billboard Hot Country Songs chart in November 1964. Smith has been nominated for 11 Grammy Awards, including eight nominations for Best Female Country Vocal Performance. She has also been nominated for one Academy of Country Music award and three Country Music Association awards.

Oasis were at No.1 on the UK chart with the compilation album Time Flies... 1994–2009. First released in June 2010 by Big Brother Recordings, the album contains all 27 UK singles released by the band between 1994 and 2009. The band kicked off their Oasis Live '25 Tour on 4 July 2025, at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales, their first show in 16 years. Time Flies... became the group's third best-selling album in the UK after (What's the Story) Morning Glory? and Definitely Maybe.

Taylor Swift was at No.1 on the UK album chart her eighth studio album Folklore. Upon release, Folklore broke the Guinness World Record for the biggest opening day on Spotify for an album by a female act. Three of its tracks reached the top 10 of the official charts in eight countries. It was Swift's seventh consecutive No.1 album on the US Billboard 200 and became the best-selling album of 2020.

US record producer Jerry Wexler, who influenced the careers of singers including Aretha Franklin, Ray Charles and Bob Dylan died at his home in Sarasota, Florida aged 91. Wexler produced the Aretha Franklin hit 'Respect', the Wilson Pickett song, 'In the Midnight Hour' and helped Bob Dylan win his first Grammy award by producing the 1979 album, Slow Train Coming. He also coined the term ‘rhythm and blues’ while writing for Billboard magazine in the late 1940s.

works.title: Whistle Down The Wind
works.artist: to have four No.1 singles. Also Boyzone became

description: Boyzone scored their fourth UK No.1 single with 'No Matter What', making them the first Irish group to have four No.1 singles. Also Boyzone became the first act in history to reach the Top 5 with their first 12 single releases. The song came from the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical 'Whistle Down The Wind'.

INXS went to No.1 on the UK chart with their eighth studio album Welcome To Whoever You Are, their first UK No.1 album, (the first album by an Australian artist to debut on the UK album chart at No.1 since AC/DC's Back in Black, released in 1980). The album featured the UK hit singles 'Heaven Sent', 'Baby Don't Cry' and 'Beautiful Girl'.

Boyz II Men started a 13 week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'End Of The Road' the group's first US No.1. Taken from the Eddie Murphy film Boomerang, it broke the 36-year-old record held by Elvis Presley for the longest run at No.1

works.title: I Just Can't Stop Loving You

description: Michael Jackson had his third UK No.1 with the single 'I Just Can't Stop Loving You', a duet with Siedah Garrett. It was originally intended to be a duet between Jackson and either Barbra Streisand or Whitney Houston. Session singer Siedah Garrett also worked with Madonna.
Diana Ross and Lionel Richie started a nine week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Endless Love', a No.7 in the UK. The song was the title from a film starring Brooke Shields.

Elvis Presley started a five week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with It’s Now or Never also No.1 in the UK. The song which was based on the Italian song, 'O Sole Mio', gave Presley his first post-army No.1.

Joe Jonas, American singer and actor, from the American pop rock band Jonas Brothers, who had the 2009 US No.1 album Lines, Vines and Trying Times. They gained popularity from their appearances on Disney Channel. They starred in the 2008 Disney Channel Original Movie Camp Rock and its 2010 sequel, Camp Rock 2: The Final Jam. They also starred in their own Disney Channel series Jonas.

American rapper, songwriter Nipsey Hussle. He initially became known for his numerous mixtapes, including his Bullets Ain't Got No Name series, The Marathon, The Marathon Continues and Crenshaw. His debut studio album Victory Lap was released in February 2018 to critical acclaim and commercial success and was nominated for Best Rap Album at the 61st Annual Grammy Awards in 2019. He died on 31 March 2019 age 33 after being shot multiple times in the parking lot of his store, Marathon Clothing, in South Los Angeles.

Ted Dwane, bassist of the Grammy Award winning British folk rock band Mumford & Sons. Their second studio album 'Babel' released in 2012 debuted at No.1 on both the UK Albums Chart and the US Billboard 200. It became the fastest selling album of 2012 in the UK. The live performance at the 2011 Grammy ceremony with Bob Dylan and The Avett Brothers led to a surge in popularity for the band in the US. The band received eight total Grammy nominations for Babel and won the Grammy Award for Album of the Year.
Tim Foreman bassist for Switchfoot. Their 2014 album Fading West reached No.6 on the US album chart.

Mike Graham, vocals, Boyzone, who have had 21 UK hit singles, including 6 UK No.1 singles. Their breakthrough hit was their second single and cover version of the classic Osmonds hit, 'Love Me for a Reason', which peaked at No.2 on the UK Singles Chart.

works.title: There's A Ghost In My House

description: British musician Marshall Schofield, keyboards, The Fall, (from 1986–1990), who had the 1987 UK No.30 single with a cover of the R. Dean Taylor hit 'There's A Ghost In My House'.

English singer-songwriter Matt Johnson best known as the lead vocalist and only constant member of his band the The who had the 1993 UK hit single 'Slow Emotion Replay'. Their second studio album, Infected, reached No. 14 in the UK Albums Chart and remained in the chart for 30 weeks.

American singer, songwriter, and musician Bobby Caldwell. He wrote many songs for other artists, including the Billboard No.1 single 'The Next Time I Fall' for Amy Grant and Peter Cetera. Caldwell died on 14 March 2023, at the age of 71.

American singer and songwriter Billy Griffin. He is best known for replacing Smokey Robinson as lead singer of The Miracles in 1972. He co-wrote the Miracles' most successful single, the No.1 hit 'Love Machine', in 1975.

American musician Tom Johnston the guitarist and vocalist, known principally as a founder and songwriter for The Doobie Brothers who have sold more than 40 million albums worldwide. They scored the 1979 US No.1 single 'What A Fool Believes' and the 1993 UK No.7 single 'Long Train Runnin.'

works.title: By the Time I Get to Phoenix

description: Jimmy Webb American singer and songwriter who wrote the 1968 hit for Richard Harris MacArthur Park, plus 'Galveston', for Glen Campbell (and other hits for Campbell), and 'Up Up and Away', a hit for 5th Dimension. According to BMI, his song 'By the Time I Get to Phoenix' was the third most performed song in the fifty years between 1940 and 1990. Webb is the only artist ever to have received Grammy Awards for music, lyrics, and orchestration.

British drummer Pete York, one of the original members of the Spencer Davis Group, along with Spencer Davis and the brothers Steve and Muff Winwood. They scored the 1966 UK No.1 single 'Keep On Running' and US Top 10 hits 'Gimme Some Lovin'' and 'I'm a Man'.

American drummer Stix Hooper, a founding member of The Crusaders, who had the 1979 UK No.5 & US No.36 single 'Street Life'. Hooper has also worked with B.B. King, Quincy Jones, Marvin Gaye, Nancy Wilson and the Rolling Stones.

works.title: Save The Last Dance For Me

description: Bill Pinkney, The Drifters, (1960 US No.1 & UK No.2 single 'Save The Last Dance For Me'). He died on July 4th 2007.

works.title: What Kind of Fool (Do You Think I Am)

description: Floyd Ashman from the American vocal group The Tams who had the 1964 US hit 'What Kind of Fool (Do You Think I Am)' and the 1971 UK No.1 single 'Hey Girl Don't Bother Me'. The group took their name from the Tam o'shanter hats they wore on stage.

A bandstand where David Bowie played soon after the release of his first hit single 'Space Oddity' was given a Grade II listing. The singer performed from the stand to a small audience in Croydon Road Recreation Ground on 16 August 1969. The bandstand was the centrepiece of a one-day festival, which Bowie helped to organise and later inspired him to write the seven-minute song, ‘Memory Of A Free Festival’.

American singer and songwriter Aretha Franklin died in Detroit at the age of 76. Known as ‘The Queen of Soul’ and one of the best-selling musical artists of all time, having sold more than 75 million records worldwide was diagnosed with cancer in 2010. During her career she scored over 15 Top 40 hits and won 18 Grammy Awards. Hits include the 1967 US No.1 & UK No.10 single 'Respect', the 1968 UK No.4 single 'I Say A Little Prayer' and the 1987 UK No.1 single with George Michael, 'I Knew You Were Waiting'. In 2010 Rolling Stone magazine ranked her number one on their list of the ‘100 Greatest Singers of All Time’.

One Direction were at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Drag Me Down'. It was the band's first single since Zayn Malik's departure earlier in this year The track won the fan-voted 'Best Video Award' at the 2016 Brit Awards.

A fan of the 1980s pop band Wham! was silenced after becoming the first noise nuisance to be prosecuted by Newcastle city council's night watch team. Brian Turner had tormented neighbours by playing their hit song 'Last Christmas' all night at full volume from 1am onwards. Magistrates fined Turner, of Sandyford, Newcastle-upon-Tyne, £200 and ordered him to pay £215 costs.

Alan Caddy guitarist with The Tornadoes died. He had the 1962 UK & US No.1 single 'Telstar' which became the first major hit from a UK act on the American chart. Caddy also played on sessions and worked on arrangements for Spencer Davis Group, Kiki Dee, Pretty Things and Dusty Springfield.
Will Smith started a four-week run at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Men In Black' taken from the film of the same name. The song won Smith a Grammy in 1997 for Best Rap Solo Performance.

Madonna started a two week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Papa Don't Preach.' The singers fourth US No.1, & No.1 in the UK. Also on this day Madonna went to No.1 on the US album chart with 'True Blue'.

works.title: Can't Give You Anything (But My Love)

description: The Stylistics were at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Can't Give You Anything (But My Love)', the Philadelphian soul group's only UK No.1.

This week's UK Top 5 singles: No.5, Free, 'All Right Now', No.4, Shirley Bassey, 'Something', No.3, Hotlegs, 'Neanderthal Man', No.2, The Kinks, 'Lola' and No.1, Elvis Presley, 'The Wonder Of You', (his 16th UK No.1).

At Abbey Road studios, The Beatles continued to work on the new George Harrison song 'While My Guitar Gently Weeps', taking the song from its early acoustic version into an electric version. The following month, Harrison asked Eric Clapton to play guitar on the track. Clapton was reluctant to participate, stating that nobody ever plays on Beatles records. Harrison convinced him, and Clapton's lead guitar part, played on Harrison's Gibson Les Paul electric guitar "Lucy" (a recent gift from Clapton), was overdubbed.

works.title: I Call It Pretty Music, (But The Old People Call It The Blues)

description: Little Stevie Wonder (aged 12), released his first single, 'I Call It Pretty Music, (But The Old People Call It The Blues)', the single featured Marvin Gaye on drums.
American singer-songwriter and pianist Venessa Carlton who had the 2002 UK No.6 single 'A Thousand Miles'. The single spent 41 weeks on the Billboard Hot 100 and earned three Grammy nominations.
MC. Remedee, from English rap music duo Cookie Crew who had the 1988 UK No.5 single 'Rock Da House'. Their career took off after winning a national rap championship.

Madonna, (Madonna Louise Veronica Ciccone), singer, actress. First hit was the 1984 UK No.6 single 'Holiday'. With sales of over 300 million records worldwide, Madonna is certified as the best-selling female recording artist of all time by Guinness World Records. She is the most successful solo artist in the history of the US Billboard Hot 100 chart and holds the record for the most No.1 singles by a female artist in Australia, Canada, Italy, Spain, and the United Kingdom.

Tim Farriss, guitarist from Australian rock band INXS, who had the 1988 UK No.2 & US No.1 single 'Need You Tonight'. Their 1987 album Kick has sold over 10m copies in the US alone and features four Top 10 singles; 'Need You Tonight,' 'Devil Inside', 'New Sensation,' and 'Never Tear Us Apart.' INXS has sold over 55 million records worldwide.
James Taylor, Kool & The Gang, who had the 1981 US No.1 & UK No.7 single, Celebration and the 1984 UK No.2 single 'Joanna', plus over 15 other top 40 hits. Taylor left the group in February 1988.

works.title: Raw Power gained a cult following

description: American musician, Scott Asheton, best known as the drummer for the rock band The Stooges. Their 1973 album Raw Power gained a cult following in the years following its release and is considered a forerunner of punk rock. Asheton died of a heart attack in March 2014 at the age of 64.

Barry Hay lead vocalist and frontman from Dutch rock band Golden Earring, who had the 1974 UK No.7 & US 13 single 'Radar Love'. The song has been chosen by many magazines and websites as a Top 10 driving song, often ranking in the top three. During their career, they had nearly 30 top-ten singles on the Dutch charts and released 25 studio albums.

Gary Loizzo, from American rock band American Breed, who scored the 1967 US No.5 single 'Bend Me, Shape Me', (a hit on the British charts for the British group Amen Corner). The band also found themselves in high demand in the lucrative radio jingles market, recording commercials for Coca-Cola, the United States Navy, and Bell Telephone, among others. Their television commercial for American Airlines ('Fly the American Way') was also a big success in the top twenty.

English-born Australian drummer Snowy Fleet, who with The Easybeats had the 1966 UK No.6 & 1967 US No. 16 single 'Friday On My Mind'. Fleet left the Easybeats in the spring of 1967. Born in Liverpool, he played drums in many Liverpool bands and sometimes shared the stage with The Beatles. Before he moved to Australia, he played in the Nomads, a band that then became the Mojos. Fleet died on 17 February 2025 at his home in Perth, aged 85.
The American baritone vocalist Al Hibbler who had the 1955 UK No.2 & US No.3 single 'Unchained Melody'. He sang with Duke Ellington's orchestra before having several pop hits as a solo artist.

ZZ Top drummer Frank Beard died aged 77. ZZ Top was founded in 1969 and played their first live concert the following year. Together they released 15 studio and four live albums, with hit singles like 'Gimme All Your Lovin'', 'Sharp Dressed Man', 'Legs and 'Viva Las Vegas'. They released 15 studio albums, sold an estimated 50 million records and won three MTV Video Music Awards, and in 2004, the members were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. ZZ Top appeared in a cameo in Back to the Future Part III as an Old West band, playing an acoustic version of their song 'Doubleback' with a large fiddle band.

American rapper Travis Scott was at No.1 on the US chart with his fourth studio album Utopia. In the UK, Utopia debuted at No.1 on the UK Albums Chart, becoming Scott's first album to achieve it. It also earned the biggest streaming week in 2023 for an album in the UK. As of 2023, Scott has sold over 49 million records in the US alone.

Jackson Browne was suing US Republican presidential candidate John McCain for using one of his songs without permission. Browne claimed the use of his song 'Running on Empty' in an advert was an infringement of copyright and would lead people to conclude he endorses McCain. Browne was seeking more than $75,000 (£40,000) in damages.

Hours before his wife was murdered, Jacksonville, Florida, resident Justin Barber downloaded the Guns N" Roses song 'Used To Love Her', (from the 1988 album G N' R Lies). The song is later played at the trial as evidence, with the lyrics displayed for the jury ("I used to love her, but I had to kill her..."). Barber was convicted of first-degree murder and given a life sentence. In addition to Barber's music, the court was told that Barber had been searching the Internet for keywords such as "trauma," "gunshot", and "right chest".

Darius was at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Colourblind'. The third "Pop Idol" finalist to get a number one. He'd originally lost out on "Popstars", failing to get a place in the group Hear'Say, and then came third in "Pop Idol".

Session drummer Gary Chester died of cancer. He had been a member of The Coasters and played on many major hits for other acts including: 'Brown Eyed Girl' 'Under The Boardwalk' 'Walk On By', 'It's My Party.'
The Rascals (formerly the Young Rascals), started a five week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'People Got To Be Free'. The group had thirteen US top 40 hits.

The Doors started a four-week run at No.1 on the US album chart with Waiting For The Sun (the band's only No.1 album), topping the Billboard 200 for four weeks. The group's third album spawned their second US No.1 single, 'Hello, I Love You'.

works.title: I Forgot to Remember to Forget / Mystery Train

description: Elvis Presley released what would become his first No.1 hit, 'I Forgot to Remember to Forget / Mystery Train'. It hit the top of the country charts several months later and stayed there for 5 weeks.
Mike Lewis, guitarist, from Welsh rock band Lostprophets, who scored the 2006 UK No.1 album Liberation Transmission.

works.title: You Got It, The Right Stuff

description: American songwriter, actor, Donnie Wahlberg, from American boy band New Kids on the Block, who had the 1989 UK No.1 single 'You Got It, The Right Stuff', and the 1990 US No.1 single 'Step By Step'. They enjoyed success in the late 1980s and early 1990s and have sold more than 80 million records worldwide.

works.title: Feel Good Inc
works.artist: won a Grammy for their collaboration with Gorillaz

description: American rapper and record producer Kelvin Mercer (also known by his stage name Posdnuos, Plug 1), from American hip hop trio De La Soul, who had the 1990 UK No.7 single 'The Magic Number'. In 2006, the group won a Grammy for their collaboration with Gorillaz on their single 'Feel Good Inc.'

works.title: The Southern Harmony And Musical Companion

description: Steve Gorman, drummer with The Black Crowes, who had the 1991 hit single 'Hard To Handle' and the 1992 US No.1 & UK No.2 album The Southern Harmony And Musical Companion. The band have sold more than 30 million albums.

American singer-songwriter Maria Mckee, (the half-sister of Bryan MacLean (1946–1998), the guitarist of the band Love). Mckee was a member of the American country rock band Lone Justice. She had the solo 1990 UK No.1 single and worldwide hit with 'Show Me Heaven' from the soundtrack to the Tom Cruise film Days of Thunder. 'A Good Heart' was written by McKee and became a hit for the Northern Irish singer Feargal Sharkey in 1985. Her song 'If Love Is a Red Dress (Hang Me in Rags)' was featured on the soundtrack to Quentin Tarantino's 1994 film Pulp Fiction. In 1987, she appeared in the Robbie Robertson music video 'Somewhere Down the Crazy River'.

works.title: Life Begins at the Hop
works.artist: XTC. Moulding wrote three of their earliest charting

description: English bassist, singer, and songwriter Colin Moulding who was one of the core members of the rock band XTC. Moulding wrote three of their earliest charting UK singles: 'Life Begins at the Hop' (1979), 'Making Plans for Nigel' (1979) and 'Generals and Majors' (1980). In 1986, David Gilmour approached Moulding about becoming Pink Floyd's new bass player following Roger Waters' departure. He turned it down, as XTC were in the midst of recording their album Skylarking (1986).

British singer and musician Kevin Rowland, from Dexy's Midnight Runners, who had the 1980 UK No.1 'Geno' and the 1982 UK No.1 & 1983 US No.1 single 'Come On Eileen ', as well as their cover of Van Morrison's 'Jackie Wilson Said (I'm in Heaven When You Smile)', which reached No. 5 in the UK. Rowland had the 1986 solo UK No.13 single 'Because Of You'.

Sib Hashian, drums, Boston, (1977 UK No.22 single 'More Than A Feeling', 1986 US No.1 single 'Amanda'). Boston have sold more than 75 million records worldwide, including 31 million albums in the United States, of which 17 million were from their self-titled debut album and seven million were for their second album, Don't Look Back, making them one of the world's best-selling artists. Hashian died on March 22, 2017, at the age of 67, after collapsing in the middle of a set while performing on board a cruise ship.

American guitarist, singer, and songwriter Gary Talley, who, with The Box Tops, had the 1967 US No.1 & UK No.5 single 'The Letter'. Talley relocated to Nashville in 1981 where he recorded with Willie Nelson, Tammy Wynette, Waylon Jennings, Sam Moore (of the duo Sam and Dave), and others.

works.title: Indian Reservation (The Lament of the Cherokee Reservation Indian)

description: American musician Drake Levin best known as the guitarist for the pop-rock band Paul Revere & the Raiders. The Raiders became a national teen sensation from their daily television exposure on the ABC television show Where The Action Is. In early 1970 the band's name was shortened to "Raiders" and one year later the hugely successful cover of the song 'Indian Reservation (The Lament of the Cherokee Reservation Indian)' reached No.1 in the US. Levin died of cancer 4 July 2009 age 62.

works.title: Sunday Will Never Be The Same Again

description: John Seiter, from American 1960s sunshine pop band Spanky And Our Gang, who had the 1967 US No.9 single 'Sunday Will Never Be The Same Again'.

works.title: X notched up eight weeks at No

description: Ed Sheeran's album X notched up eight weeks at No.1 on the UK chart, becoming the joint longest chart-topper by a male solo artist. The last man to achieve the feat was James Blunt for his 2005 collection Back to Bedlam.

works.title: San Francisco (Be Sure to Wear Flowers in Your Hair)

description: American singer and songwriter Scott McKenzie died aged 73. He was best known for his 1967 hit single and generational anthem, 'San Francisco (Be Sure to Wear Flowers in Your Hair)'. He also joined a new version of The Mamas & the Papas and co-wrote "Kokomo" (1988), a No.1 single for The Beach Boys.

works.title: Working My Way Back To You

description: Soul singer Pervis Jackson died of cancer. Was a member of The Spinners (Also known as The Motown Spinners and The Detroit Spinners). Had the 1980 UK No.1 & US No.2 single 'Working My Way Back To You'.
Tony Jackson bass player with The Searchers died of cirrhosis of the liver. The Searchers had the 1964 UK No.1 & US No.13 single 'Needles And Pins'.

George Michael was at No.1 on the UK singles chart with his first solo single 'Careless Whisper.' It made George the first person to reach No.1 as a solo artist and a member of a band in the same year. It gave Epic records UK their first UK million seller and the song was No.1 in nearly 25 countries, selling over six million copies worldwide.

works.title: Good Times
works.artist: Chic went to No.1 on the US singles

description: American R&B band Chic went to No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Good Times', the first single from their third album, Risqué (1979). Written and produced by Bernard Edwards and Nile Rodgers, 'Good Times' has become one of the most sampled songs in music history, most notably in hip-hop music.

Diana Ross scored her second US No.1 single with 'Touch Me In The Morning'. The song marked a turning point in her career, coming immediately after her Academy Award nomination for Best Actress in her acting debut, Lady Sings the Blues.

Lebanese singer-songwriter Mika, (Mica Penniman), who scored the 2007 UK No.1 single 'Grace Kelly'. His 2007 UK No.1 album Life in Cartoon Motion sold more than 8 million copies worldwide and helped Mika win a Brit Award in 2008 for Best British Breakthrough act, while its single 'Love Today' was nominated for a Grammy Award.

Canadian multi-instrumentalist and singer, Régine Chassagne, founding member of Arcade Fire. (She is married to co-founder Win Butler). Had the 2005 album Funeral, and 2017 US No.1 album Everything Now.

British musician, composer and DJ Richard James, known professionally as Aphex Twin. His 2014 album Syro peaked at No.8 on the UK chart and No.1 on the US Dance chart and won a Grammy Award for Best Dance/Electronic Album.
Erik Schrody, Irish-American rapper and singer-songwriter, House Of Pain, (1993 UK No.3 single 'Jump Around'). Member of Everlast, (1999 UK No. 34 single 'What It's Like').

British singer Tracy Tracy, from English indie pop band Primitives who scored the 1988 UK No.5 single 'Crash'. They received valuable publicity when the The Smiths' lead vocalist Morrissey was photographed wearing a Primitives T-shirt.

Australian musician Ron Strykert, from Men at Work. They were best known for breakthrough hits such as 'Down Under', and 'Who Can It Be Now?' In January 1983, they were the first Australian artists to have a simultaneous No. 1 album and No. 1 single on the United States Billboard charts: Business as Usual (released on 9 November 1981) and 'Down Under' (1981), respectively.

works.title: Shout
works.artist: The Isley Brothers who first came to prominence in

works.title: Twist and Shout
works.artist: The Isley Brothers who first came to prominence in

works.title: This Old Heart Of Mine
works.artist: The Isley Brothers who first came to prominence in

description: Marvin Isley from American group The Isley Brothers who first came to prominence in 1959 with their fourth single, 'Shout', and then the 1962 hit 'Twist and Shout'. The Isley Brothers also scored the hits 'This Old Heart Of Mine', 'Summer Breeze' and 'Harvest for the World'. Sixteen of their albums charted in the Top 40. Marvin Isley died from complications of diabetes on June 6, 2010.
Patrick Swayze, actor, singer, (1988 US No.3 & UK No.17 single with Wendy Fraser, 'She's Like The Wind'). Swayze died from pancreatic cancer on September 14, 2009.

John Rees from Australian rock band Men at Work. They were best known for breakthrough hits such as 'Down Under', and 'Who Can It Be Now?' In January 1983, they were the first Australian artists to have a simultaneous No. 1 album and No. 1 single on the United States Billboard charts: Business as Usual (released on 9 November 1981) and 'Down Under' (1981), respectively.

Nigel Griggs bassist from New Zealand group Split Enz who had the 1980 UK No.12 single 'I Got You'. Split Enz had ten albums (including seven studio albums) reach the top ten of the Official New Zealand Music Chart.

Barbara Harris, singer with the American pop girl group from Jamaica, New York, The Toys, who had the 1965 US No. 2 & UK No.5 single 'A Lover's Concerto'. They had a cameo role performing their song 'Attack!' in the 1967 beach movie It's a Bikini World.

American singer and actress Sarah Dash, who with Labelle had the 1975 US No.1 & UK No.17, single 'Lady Marmalade'. She worked as a singer, session musician, and sideman for The Rolling Stones, and Keith Richards. Dash died unexpectedly on 20 September 2021 at the age of 76.

works.title: I Can Hear The Grass Grow

description: Carl Wayne, singer, with British rock band The Move who had the 1969 UK No.1 single 'Blackberry Way' and hits with 'I Can Hear The Grass Grow', 'Flowers in the Rain' and 'Fire Brigade'. Wayne died of cancer on 31st Aug 2004.
American soul and R&B singer Maxine Brown. She recorded a string of sizable hits for Wand Records in the mid 60s. Among these were the Carole King/Gerry Goffin songs 'Oh No Not My Baby'.
American pop singer Johnny Preston, best known for his 1960 US & UK No.1 single 'Running Bear'. Preston died of heart failure on 4 March 4 2011.

A life-size bronze statue designed by Paul Daly of Phil Lynott was unveiled on Harry Street in Dublin. The ceremony was attended by his former Thin Lizzy band members Gary Moore, Brian Robertson and Scott Gorham. Lynott who died in 1986 aged 36 had a string of hits including 'Whiskey in the Jar', 'The Boys are Back in Town', 'Jailbreak' and 'Waiting for an Alibi'.

works.title: The Shoop Shoop Song (It's In His Kiss

description: American soul singer Betty Everett died aged 61. She had the 1964 US No.6 single 'The Shoop Shoop Song (It's In His Kiss'). In 1984, the song was used for the opening credits in the Madonna film Desperately Seeking Susan. In 1990, the song had a cover version in Mermaids for the end credits, and was recorded by the star of the film, Cher. This reached No. 1 in the UK Singles Chart and charted well elsewhere in Europe.

works.title: Once, Twice, Three Times a Lady

description: The Commodores started a five-week run at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Three Times A Lady'. Lionel Richie wrote the song about his love for his wife, mother and grandmother hence 'Once, Twice, Three Times a Lady.'

works.title: When Will I See You Again

description: The Three Degrees were at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'When Will I See You Again.' The girl group's only UK No.1. The Three Degrees performed the song at Charles III's 30th birthday party at Buckingham Palace in 1978 (when he was known as Prince Charles) as he had stated that the song was a favourite of his.

American singers Rita Coolidge and Kris Kristofferson were married in Malibu, California. Kristofferson had just enjoyed a number 1 country hit with 'Why Me', which included Coolidge on backing vocals. Coolidge first met Kristofferson at the Los Angeles airport when they were both catching the same flight to Tennessee. Instead of continuing to his intended destination in Nashville, he got off in Memphis with her. The couple divorced near the end of 1979.
Missy Higgins, Australian singer-songwriter, (2004 Australian No.1 single ‘Scar’, 2007 Australian No.1 single 'Steer').

Darius, singer, 2001 UK TV's Popstars contestant, who became famous for his rendition of Britney Spears 'Baby One More Time' and scored the 2002 UK No.1 single 'Colourblind'. He later performed the role of Billy Flynn in the West End production of Chicago and played the lead role of Sky Masterson in Guys and Dolls. Darius was found unresponsive on 11 August 2022 in his apartment in Rochester, Minnesota, and he was pronounced dead later that day.
MC Eric, from Belgian electronic music project Technotronic, who had the 1989 UK No.2 single 'Pump Up The Jam' and was a worldwide hit, reaching No.2 on the US Billboard Hot 100 in early 1990.

Swedish musician Joey Tempest (Rolf Larsson), the lead vocalist of the rock band Europe, who had the 1986 UK No.1 single 'The Final Countdown'. Larsson started performing in 1979, creating the stage name "Joey Tempest", inspired by William Shakespeare's tragicomedy The Tempest as well as the song 'Sparks of the Tempest' by American progressive rock band Kansas.

John Deacon, bass, Queen. He was the last to join the band and also the youngest, being only 19 years old. Deacon wrote a number of Queen's hit singles, including 'You're My Best Friend', 'Spread Your Wings', 'I Want to Break Free', and the band's biggest selling single in the United States, 'Another One Bites the Dust'.

English singer and songwriter Ian Gillan from Deep Purple, who had the 1970 UK No.2 single 'Black Night' and the 1973 US No. 4 single 'Smoke On The Water'. Gillan has also been a member of Episode Six, Ian Gillan Band, Gillan, Black Sabbath, Gillan & Glover and WhoCares.

English pop singer Billy J Kramer, who had the 1964 UK No.1 & US No.7 single 'Little Children'. With the Dakotas, Kramer was managed by Brian Epstein during the 1960s and scored hits with several Lennon–McCartney compositions never recorded by The Beatles, among them the UK No.1 'Bad to Me' (1963).

American singer-songwriter Johnny Nash, who had the 1972 US No.1 single 'I Can See Clearly Now', and the 1975 UK No.1 single 'Tears On My Pillow'. Nash died of natural causes on 6 October 2020 age 80.

Roger Cook, songwriter, as a member of Blue Mink, (1970 UK No.3 single 'Melting Pot'). Cook has had more than 80 top 30 hits, including ‘Something’s Gotten Hold Of My Heart’, ‘Long Cool Woman In A Black Dress’ , ‘You’ve Got Your Troubles’ and ‘I’d Like To Teach The World To Sing.’

Ginger Baker, drummer with Cream who had the 1966 UK No.11 single 'I Feel Free'. Baker was also a member of the Graham Bond Organisation, Blind Faith, and Ginger Bakers Airforce and is also known for his numerous associations with World music, mainly the use of African influences. He has also had other collaborations such as with Gary Moore, Hawkwind and Public Image Ltd. Baker died on 6 October at the age of 80.

American musician Brent Hinds was killed when a BMW SUV hit his motorcycle in Atlanta, Georgia. Police estimated that Hinds was travelling between 63 and 68 mph at the time of the crash, roughly twice the speed limit. Hinds was best known as the lead guitarist and one of the vocalists of the Atlanta heavy metal band Mastodon. Their 2014 album Once More 'Round the Sun peaked at No. 6 on the Billboard 200 chart and features the band's third Grammy-nominated song, 'High Road'.

works.title: Kryptonite
works.artist: rose to international fame with their first single

description: Former 3 Doors Down guitarist Matt Roberts died at the age of 38 from a prescription drug overdose. The American rock band rose to international fame with their first single, 'Kryptonite', which charted in the top three on the Billboard chart. The released their debut album, The Better Life, in 2000 which became the 11th-best-selling album of the year and was certified 6x platinum in the United States.

Spiller went to No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Groovejet'. The Italian DJ and producer mixed the track based on an old 1970s hit 'Love Is You' by Carol Williams, with new vocals by Sophie Ellis-Bextor.
Janet Jackson went to No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Doesn't Really Matter'. Nelly started a five week run at No.1 on the US album chart with 'Country Grammar'.

Bob Dylan released his nineteenth studio album, Slow Train Coming. It was Dylan's first album following his conversion to Christianity, and the songs either express personal faith or stress the importance of Christian teachings and philosophy. The set included the Grammy Award-winning single, 'Gotta Serve Somebody'. The album alienated many of his long-time fans.

works.title: You've Got a Habit of Leaving

description: Davy Jones & The Lower Third released the single 'You've Got a Habit of Leaving' the last song that David Bowie (born David Jones), released before changing his name to avoid confusion with Davy Jones of The Monkees, and the first of two singles that he recorded with The Lower Third after leaving his previous band, The Manish Boys.
Jamie Cullum, UK Jazz, singer, songwriter, instrumentalist, (2003 UK No.5 album 'Twentysomething').

works.title: Chocolate Starfish and the Hotdog Flavoured Water

description: Fred Durst, vocals, Limp Bizkit, (2001 UK No.1 single 'Rollin' & 2000 US & UK No.1 album 'Chocolate Starfish and the Hotdog Flavoured Water').

Dimebag Darrell, guitarist, Pantera, (1994 UK No.19 single 'I'm Broken'). Darrell was killed on 8th December 2004 after a man stormed the stage during a Damageplan show at the Alrosa Villa Club in Columbus, Ohio and began firing shots at the band and crowd.

American singer-songwriter-musician Doug Fieger, with The Knack. Their first single, 'My Sharona' was an international No.1 hit in 1979. Fieger wrote 'My Sharona' for Sharona Alperin, who later became his girlfriend. He died of cancer on 14th Feb 2010 aged 57.

Phil Lynott, Irish singer, songwriter, bass player, Thin Lizzy. (1973 UK No.6 single 'Whisky In The Jar'). Lynott died on 4th Jan 1986 of heart failure and pneumonia after being in a coma for eight days following a drug overdose. A life-size bronze statue of Phil Lynott was unveiled on Harry Street in Dublin in 2005.

American trombone player, songwriter, James Pankow, with Chicago who had the 1976 UK & US No.1 single 'If You Leave Me Now'. The band formed in 1967 in Chicago, Illinois as The Chicago Transit Authority before shortening the name in 1970. Chicago have had five consecutive No.1 albums on the Billboard chart and 20 top-ten singles on the Billboard Hot 100.

German musician and composer Ralf Hutter, from the German electronic music and pop band Kraftwerk who had the 1982 UK No.1 single 'Computer Love / The Model'. Kraftwerk are widely considered innovators and pioneers of electronic music and were among the first successful acts to popularise the genre. Their commercially successful albums such as Autobahn (1974), Trans-Europe Express (1977), The Man-Machine (1978), and Computer World (1981), Kraftwerk developed a self-described "robot pop" style that combined electronic music with pop melodies, sparse arrangements, and repetitive rhythms, while adopting a stylised image including matching suits.
Isaac Hayes, singer, (1971 US No.1 & UK No.4 single, 'Theme From Shaft', 1998 UK No.2 single as Chef 'Chocolate Salty Balls'). Hayes was found dead at his home on 10th Aug 2008, aged 65.
English singer-songwriter and musician Dave Brock best known as being one of the founders of space rock group Hawkwind who had the 1972 UK No.3 single 'Silver Machine'.

English rock and roll drummer Clem Cattini with The Tornadoes who had the 1962 UK & US No.1 single 'Telstar'. The first major hit from a UK act on the American chart. Cattini has featured on a record 44 different UK No.1 singles, from artists such as Tom Jones, T. Rex, The Seekers, Bay City Rollers, Rolf Harris and Hot Chocolate. He was also considered for Led Zeppelin – he was initially on Jimmy Page's shortlist of drummers when forming the band before they settled on John Bonham.

Paul Robi, from American vocal group The Platters who had the 1959 UK & US No.1 single 'Smoke Gets In Your Eyes'. The Platters were one of the first African-American groups to be accepted as a major chart group and were, for a period of time, the most successful vocal group in the world. He died of cancer on 1st February 1989.

Jim Reeves US country singer. The first country singer to crossover into the pop market. (1960 US No.2 single 'He'll Have To Go', 1966 UK No.1 single 'Distant Drums'). Reeves was killed in a plane crash on 31st July 1964 when the single engine aircraft flying from Arkansas to Nashville crashed in thick fog.

Handwritten lyrics and chord charts for one of Fleetwood Mac's earliest hits sold for £24,700 at auction. The composition sheet for the band's 1969 UK No.2 hit 'Man of the World' was written by the group's co-founder, vocalist and lead guitarist Peter Green. The song sheet, handwritten in blue ballpoint pen and corrected in black ink, showed that Green changed three lines of the lyrics, adding a complete line to the last verse, while confirming his choice for others by annotating the end of each finalised line with a tick.

Police in Ohio raided the home of singer Afroman looking for evidence of kidnapping and drug trafficking. He wasn't charged, and used the surveillance footage in the video for his song 'Lemon Pound Cake,' zeroing in on a moment when an officer looks down to discover the cake in the kitchen. The search damaged his door, external gate, and security system wiring, which cost over $20,000 to repair. During the raid officers also seized over $5,000 of cash from his home. The cash was later returned to him but with $400 missing.

Don Everly, the surviving member of the rock 'n' roll duo The Everly Brothers, died at the age of 84. Everly and his brother, Phil, had worldwide hits in the late 1950s and early 1960s, including 'Bye Bye Love' and 'All I Have To Do Is Dream'. They were known for their close harmonies, and influenced groups like The Beatles and Simon and Garfunkel. The Beatles based the vocal arrangement of 'Please Please Me' on The Everly's hit 'Cathy's Clown'.

works.title: Never Gonna Give You Up
works.artist: responded by driving a truck in front of

description: After the Westboro Baptist Church, famous for their anti-gay demonstrations, staged a protest before a Foo Fighters concert in Kansas City, the band responded by driving a truck in front of the demonstrators and Rickrolling them by blasting a version of Rick Astley's hit 'Never Gonna Give You Up.'

Terence Trent D'Arby, not heard from since his 1995 album Vibrator, posted on his website: "I am a holographic representation in the third dimension of what was requested by your souls that one of your favourite artists be. I sent a portion of my soul to embody as an artist called Terence Trent D'Arby to favour that request." He later explained that he was using a new name: Sananda Maitreya, which came to him in a dream.

Oasis' third album 'Be Here Now', became one of the fastest selling albums ever, shifting over 350,000 units on the first day of release. The cover image for Be Here Now was shot at Stocks House in Hertfordshire, the former home of Victor Lownes, the head of the Playboy Clubs in the UK.

Tommy James and The Shondells returned to the UK No.1 position for the second time with the single 'Mony Mony'. In a peculiar twist, in 1987 Billy Idol's version of the song replaced another Tommy James hit at No.1 on the Billboard Hot 100 — 'I Think We're Alone Now', covered by Tiffany.

Tamla Records released the Marvelettes first single, 'Please Mr. Postman'. The song went on to sell over a million copies and become the group's biggest hit, reaching the top of both the Billboard Pop and R&B charts. The song is notable as the first Motown song to reach the No.1 position on the Billboard Hot 100 pop singles chart.

Patsy Cline recorded the classic Willie Nelson, ‘Crazy’. Cline was still on crutches after going through a car windshield in a head-on collision two months earlier and had difficulty reaching the high notes of the song at first due to her broken ribs. 'Crazy' spent 21 weeks on the chart and eventually became one of her signature tunes.
American singer and actress Melissa Schman, who, with Dream, had the 2001 US No.3 & UK No.17 single 'He Loves You Not'.

American singer Kelis Rogers, who had the 2000 UK No.4 single 'Caught Out There'. She has collaborated with R&B and hip-hop acts including Nas (whom she married in 2003), Busta Rhymes, Outkast, and Puff Daddy; electronic and dance producers such as Calvin Harris, Disclosure, Giorgio Moroder, and pop and rock acts Enrique Iglesias, Duran Duran, and No Doubt.

English musician, producer, songwriter, and DJ Liam Howlett, from the electronic dance music group The Prodigy, one of the most successful electronic groups of all time, selling an estimated 25 million records worldwide. They scored the 1996 UK No.1 & US No. 30 single 'Firestarter' and the 1997 UK & US No.1 album The Fat Of The Land. Howlett has been married to Natalie Appleton of All Saints since 2002.

English singer and songwriter Dina Carroll. She had a string of hits during the 1990s, including the UK top ten singles 'It's Too Late' (1991), 'Don't Be a Stranger' (1993), 'The Perfect Year' (1993), and 'Escaping' (1996). Carroll released two studio albums, So Close (1993) and Only Human (1996), both of which reached No.2 on the UK Albums Chart and were certified platinum. She won Best British Female Solo Artist at the 1994 Brit Awards.

works.title: Toxicity
works.artist: System of a Down who had the

works.title: Mezmerize
works.artist: System of a Down who had the

description: Serj Tankian, singer with Armenian-American heavy metal band System of a Down who had the 2001 US No.1 album Toxicity and the 2005 US No.1 & UK No.2 album Mezmerize.

American disc jockey, record producer and remixer David Morales. He has remixed and produced over 500 releases for artists including Mariah Carey, Aretha Franklin, Michael Jackson, Janet Jackson, Spice Girls, Eric Clapton, Seal, Pet Shop Boys, U2, Donna Summer, Whitney Houston, Tina Turner, Madonna, and Jamiroquai. Morales was nominated for his first Grammy Award in 1996 as a producer for the song 'Daydream Interlude (Fantasy Sweet Dub Mix)' on Mariah Carey's album Daydream. He was nominated again the next year and won the 1998 Grammy Award for "Remixer of the Year".

English drummer Budgie, (Peter Clarke), best known for his work in Siouxsie and the Banshees. Their debut single 'Hong Kong Garden' (1978) became a high-charting release peaking at No.7 in the UK, and they had the 1983 UK No.3 single with a cover of The Beatles 'Dear Prudence'). He is the co-founder of The Creatures (1983 UK No.14 single 'Right Now') and was the drummer in the Slits in 1979. They have been cited as an influence by bands such as Joy Division, The Cure, U2, Radiohead and Jeff Buckley.
Nick Kane from the American band The Mavericks who had the 1998 UK No.4 single 'Dance The Night Away'. The Mavericks won a Grammy Award for the song 'Here Comes the Rain'.

American drummer Steve Smith, who, with Journey, had the 1982 US No.2 single 'Open Arms'. Modern Drummer magazine readers have voted him the No. 1 All-Around Drummer five years in a row. Smith has worked as a session musician for Mariah Careyy, Andrea Bocelli, Zucchero, Savage Garden, Bryan Adams and others.

Turkish-born English musician, singer, actor and songwriter Joe Strummer who was the co-founder of The Clash, who had the 1979 UK No. 11 single 'London Calling' and the 1982 US No. 8 single 'Rock The Casbah. Their 1991 UK No.1 single Should I Stay Or Should I Go was first released in 1982. He later formed Joe Strummer & The Mescaleros. He died on 22nd December 2002 of an undiagnosed congenital heart defect.
Carl Giammarese, guitarist with American Sunshine pop group The Buckinghams who had the 1967 US No.1 single 'Kind Of A Drag' and became one of the top selling US acts of 1967.

American singer Clydie King, best known for her session work as a backing vocalist. She was a member of Ray Charles' Raelettes for three years and contributed to early 1960s recordings by producer Phil Spector, such as Ike and Tina Turner's 'River Deep – Mountain High'. King also recorded solo under her name. In the 1970s, she recorded as Brown Sugar, (1973 single 'Loneliness (Will Bring Us Together Again)'. King died on 7 January 2019.

works.title: Put A Little Love In Your Heart

description: American singer-songwriter and radio broadcaster Jackie DeShannon. Her biggest break came in 1964 when she supported The Beatles on their first US tour. She had the 1969 US No.4 single 'Put A Little Love In Your Heart'. She is also known for the hit 'What the World Needs Now Is Love' and 'Put a Little Love in Your Heart', and as the writer of 'When You Walk in the Room' and 'Bette Davis Eyes', which became hits for The Searchers and Kim Carnes, respectively.

British singer Cliff Adams. He led the Cliff Adams Singers known for ballads and novelty songs and formed The Stargazers that had two UK No.1 singles, 'Broken Wings' in 1953 (which was the first recording by a native British act to top the UK Singles Chart) and the 1954 'I See the Moon'. Adams wnet on to write many TV jingles, such as ads for Murray Mints, Fry's Turkish Delight, Milk Tray and Smash instant mashed potato.

Marjorie "Margie" Latzko, from the American female vocal quartet The Chordettes, died at the age of 96. They are best known for their 1950s hit singles and 'Lollipop', both of which sold over a million copies. Released in late 1954, 'Mr. Sandman' went on to become a US No.1 hit for seven weeks and has been featured in scenes of several TV shows and movies throughout the years, including Halloween II (1981), Uncle Buck (1989), Sleepy Hollow (2013), Deadpool (2016), and Stranger Things (2016).
Brian Travers, British saxophonist with UB40, died from cancer age 62. With UB40 he had the 1983 UK No.1 & 1988 US No.1 single 'Red Red Wine' and over 30 other UK top 40 hits.

Songwriter and producer Jerry Leiber died at his home in Los Angeles at the age of 78 from cardio-pulmonary failure. With Mike Stoller he wrote many hits including: 'Hound Dog', 'Jailhouse Rock', 'King Creole', 'There Goes My Baby', 'Searchin', 'Yakety Yak', 'Stand By Me', 'Poison Ivy,' and 'Kansas City'.

works.title: You're All I Need To Get By
Ain't Nothing Like the Real Thing

description: Nicholas Ashford, one half of Ashford and Simpson died of complications from throat cancer, in New York. With his wife Valerie Simpson they had the 1979 US No.36 single 'Found A Cure', and 1985 UK No. 3 single 'Solid'. The pair wrote hits such as: 'Ain't No Mountain High Enough', 'You're All I Need To Get By', 'Ain't Nothing Like the Real Thing', and 'Reach Out and Touch (Somebody's Hand)'.
Former Spice Girl Geri Halliwell scored her first UK No.1 solo single with 'Mi Chico Latino' the second single from her debut solo album Schizophonic.

Led Zeppelin's last album In Through the Out Door was released in the US. Zeppelin’s eighth studio album, would be their final full-length recording together. A little over a year later, drummer John Bonham would tragically pass away, resulting in the group’s disbandment. Recorded over three weeks in November and December 1978 at ABBA’s Polar Studios in Stockholm, the album became a massive hit, thanks in part to such enduring favourites as 'All My Love' and 'Fool in the Rain.' In addition to topping the charts on both sides of the Atlantic, the album has since been certified 6x Platinum by the RIAA.

Creedence Clearwater Revival started a nine-week run at No.1 on the US album chart with their fifth studio album Cosmo's Factory. The name of the album comes from the warehouse in Berkeley where the band rehearsed. Bandleader John Fogerty was so insistent on practising (nearly every day) that drummer Doug "Cosmo" Clifford began referring to the place as "the factory".

The Beatles met at John Lennon's Tittenhurst Park home in England for their final ever photo session. Three shots from this session (by Ethan Russell) formed the front and back covers of the Capitol compilation album Hey Jude. Yoko Ono and a pregnant Linda McCartney (she was to give birth to daughter Mary six days later) appeared in some photographs with The Beatles.

The Supremes started a two week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Where Did Our Love Go' the girl group's first No.1. Holland–Dozier–Holland had originally composed the song for The Marvelettes to record it who rejected the song.

Billy J Kramer And The Dakotas were at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Bad To Me.' A song John Lennon wrote for them while on holiday in Spain with Brian Epstein. The track later became the first Lennon–McCartney composition to reach the US Top 40 for an artist other than The Beatles.

English singer, and songwriter Dua Lipa. Her self-titled debut studio album released in 2017 produced seven singles, including the top-ten single 'Be the One' and the No.1 single 'New Rules'. Lipa's second album, Future Nostalgia (2020), became her first UK No.1 album and won the Brit Award for British Album of the Year and the Grammy Award for Best Pop Vocal Album. She has won numerous accolades throughout her career including seven Brit Awards and three Grammy Awards.

works.title: Marchin’ Already
works.artist: Ocean Colour Scene who formed in Moseley

works.title: The Day We Caught The Train
works.artist: Ocean Colour Scene who formed in Moseley

description: Steve Cradock, guitarist with English rock band Ocean Colour Scene who formed in Moseley, Birmingham in 1989. They scored the 1996 UK No.4 single 'The Day We Caught The Train', plus over 12 other Top 40 singles and the 1997 UK No.1 album Marchin’ Already. Cradock is also a member of Paul Weller's Band.

American R&B/soul singer James Debarge, who, with the singing family vocal group Debarge, had the 1985 UK No.4 single 'Rhythm Of The Night'. DeBarge married singer Janet Jackson in 1984. The marriage was annulled in 1985. In 2012, DeBarge was imprisoned after being arrested for assault with a deadly weapon and drug charges. He was released from prison three years later.

American singer-songwriter and pianist Tori Amos who had the 1994 UK No.4 single 'Cornflake Girl'. Amos won a full scholarship to the Peabody Institute at Johns Hopkins University at the age of five, the youngest person ever to have been admitted. She was expelled at the age of 11 for "musical insubordination". Her 1996 hit 'Professional Widow' is widely rumoured to be about Courtney Love.
Debbie Peterson, drummer with American all-female band The Bangles, who had the 1986 UK No.2 single with the Prince song, 'Manic Monday' and the 1986 US No.1 single 'Walk Like An Egyptian'.

works.title: Everybody Wants To Rule The World
