Phil Collins was at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'A Groovy Kind Of Love.' Taken from his film Buster the song had been a No.2 hit for The Mindbenders in 1966. The song was written by Carole Bayer Sager when she was a 22-year-old schoolteacher, and Toni Wine who was a 17-year-old high school student.
Former Stevie Wonder guitarist Michael Sembello, started a two week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Maniac'. The track was featured in the film 'Flashdance'. A No.43 hit in the UK.
The BBC banned The Rolling Stones single 'Star Star', from their Goat's Head Soup album because it contained the word "Star-fucker" in the chorus a dozen times.

Lynn Anderson recorded 'Rose Garden' at the Columbia Recording Studios in Nashville. Anderson's version of 'Rose Garden' remains one of the most successful country crossover recordings of all-time. The track topped the US Billboard country chart for five weeks, reached No.3 on the US Billboard Hot 100 pop chart and was a major hit in Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Ireland, Norway and the UK.

The Supremes started a two week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'You Can't Hurry Love', the group's seventh US No.1. Written and produced by Motown's main production team, Holland–Dozier–Holland it peaked at No.3 in the UK and sixteen years later gave Phil Collins a UK No.1 in 1982.

The Byrds begin recording ‘Turn! Turn! Turn!’. Unlike their first hit, ‘Mr. Tambourine Man’, members of the group itself were permitted to play instead of session musicians. Written by American singer, songwriter, musician, and social activist Pete Seeger, the song was originally released in 1962 as 'To Everything There Is a Season' on the folk group the Limeliters' album Folk Matinee, and then some months later on Seeger's own album The Bitter and the Sweet.

The Kinks third single, 'You Really Got Me', was at No.1 on the UK singles chart. The song was the Kinks' breakthrough hit, establishing them as one of the top British Invasion acts in the United States. The song's novel use of power chords and distortion heavily influenced later rock musicians, particularly in the heavy metal and punk rock genres.

works.title: I Wanna Be Your Man
works.artist: were in need of material for a single

description: During a chance meeting in the street between The Rolling Stones and Paul McCartney and John Lennon, and hearing that the group were in need of material for a single, Lennon and McCartney went to their session at De Lane Lea Studio and finished off a new song 'I Wanna Be Your Man', whose verse they had already been working on – in the corner of the room while the impressed Rolling Stones watched. Released as their second single on 1 November 1963, the Stones' version was the group's first UK top-20 hit, peaking at No. 12 on the British chart.
The BBC banned Bobby 'Boris' Pickett and the Crypt Kickers single 'Monster Mash' saying it was offensive. The single went on to be a UK No.3 hit in 1973.
American rapper, singer, and songwriter Sheck Wes, best known for his 2018 single 'Mo Bamba', which went viral and peaked at No.6 on the Billboard Hot 100.
Matthew Johnson, from British boy band One True Voice, created on the ITV television series Popstars: The Rivals who had the 2002 UK No.2 single 'Sacred Trust / After You're Gone'.

works.title: Because Of The Times
works.artist: Kings of Leon who had the

description: Matthew Followill, lead guitarist, from American rock band Kings of Leon who had the 2007 UK No.1 album Because Of The Times, and the 2008 UK No.1 single ‘Sex on Fire’. The band has sold over 21 million albums worldwide and 38 million singles.

American musician and songwriter, Mikey Way best known as the bassist of the rock band My Chemical Romance, who had the 2006 UK No.1 single ‘Welcome to the Black Parade’, and the 2006 US No.2 album The Black Parade. They are considered one of the most influential rock groups of the 2000s and a major act in the emo and pop-punk genres, despite the band rejecting the former label.
Robin Goodridge, of the rock band Bush who had the 1997 UK No.7 single 'Swallowed'. The bands debut album, Sixteen Stone sold over 7 million copies in the US.

Carol Decker, vocals, T'Pau, who had the 1987 UK No.1 single 'China In Your Hand' and the 1987 US & UK No.4 single 'Heart And Soul', (which was initially a flop in the UK). T'Pau took their name from a Vulcan elder of the same name in the sci-fi series Star Trek.

Siobhan Fahey, singer with British female pop group Bananarama who had the 1984 UK No.3 single 'Robert De Niro's Waiting', plus over 20 other UK Top 40 singles, and the 1986 US No.1 single 'Venus' a cover of the Dutch rock band Shocking Blue 1970 hit. Fahey was also a member of Shakespeares Sister who had the 1992 UK No.1 single 'Stay'.

Irish keyboardist and co-founding member of the new wave band the Boomtown Rats Johnnie 'Fingers' Moylett. They are best known for the 1979 UK No.1 single 'I Don't Like Mondays', as well as a series of Irish and UK hits including 'Like Clockwork', 'Rat Trap' and 'Banana Republic'.

Pat Mastelotto, drummer, from American pop rock band Mr Mister who scored the 1985 US No.1 & 1986 UK No.4 single 'Broken Wings'. Mastelotto has also worked with King Crimson, Al Jarreau, The Pointer Sisters, Patti LaBelle, Kenny Loggins, Martika and others.

works.title: I Don't Want To Miss A Thing

description: Joe Perry, guitarist with Aerosmith who scored the 1989 UK No.13 single 'Love In An Elevator', and their 1989 album Pump spent 53 weeks on the US charts They had the 1993 US No.1 & UK No.2 album Get A Grip and the 1998 US No.1 & UK No.4 single 'I Don't Want To Miss A Thing'. Aerosmith is the best-selling American hard rock band of all time, having sold more than 150 million records worldwide.

Puerto Rican musician, singer and composer Jose Feliciano, best known for many international hits, including his rendition of The Doors' 'Light My Fire'. His 1968 album Feliciano! reached No. 2 on the US charts. Jose was born blind as a result of congenital glaucoma.

works.title: Mama Told Me Not To Come

description: Danny Hutton, singer with Three Dog Night, who had the 1970 UK No.3 & US No.1 single with a cover of the Randy Newman song 'Mama Told Me Not To Come'. The band scored 21 Billboard Top 40 hits (with three hitting No.1) between 1969 and 1975.

The Rolling Stones album Goats Head Soup was at No.1 on the UK chart. The 11th British and 13th American studio album by the Stones first released on 31 August 1973 had been remixed by Giles Martin for this 2020 reissue, including a deluxe edition with bonus tracks and unreleased outtakes.

Toots Hibbert, frontman of the legendary reggae band Toots and the Maytals, died age 77 after being taken to hospital with Covid-like symptoms. One of Jamaica’s most influential musicians, he helped popularise reggae in the 1960s with songs like 'Pressure Drop', 'Monkey Man' and 'Funky Kingston'. He even claimed to have coined the genre’s name, on 1968’s 'Do The Reggay'.

Mark Ronson’s hit Uptown Funk became the fifth biggest-selling single in British chart history with over two million UK sales and overtaking Paul McCartney & Wings’ 1977 chart-topper 'Mull Of Kintrye/Girls’ School'.

American songwriter, singer, manager, and record producer Bob Crewe died aged 83. Crewe wrote a string of Top 10 singles for the Four Seasons, including 'Big Girls Don't Cry', 'Walk Like a Man', and 'Rag Doll'. He also had hit recordings with Lesley Gore, Michael Jackson, Bobby Darin, Roberta Flack, Peabo Bryson, Patti LaBelle, Barry Manilow and others.

Mariah Carey started an eight-week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Dreamlover'. The song was eventually displaced by Meat Loaf's 'I'd Do Anything for Love (But I Won't Do That)'. Also on the same day, her third album Music Box went to No.1 in the UK. Also a US No.1 album, Music Box spent 128 weeks on the US chart, including 31 weeks in the top ten.

Reggae star Peter Tosh was tragically murdered in Kingston, Jamaica. Tosh rose to fame as a founding member of The Wailers, alongside Bob Marley and Bunny Wailer. After leaving the group in the mid-70s, Tosh established a successful solo career. In 1978, the Rolling Stones' record label, Rolling Stones Records, contracted with Tosh, on which the album Bush Doctor was released, introducing Tosh to a larger audience. The album featured Rolling Stones frontmen Mick Jagger and Keith Richards, and the lead single – a cover version of the Temptations song 'Don't Look Back'.
Chicago started a two week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Hard To Say I'm Sorry', the group's second US No.1. Taken from the film 'Summer Lovers', a No.4 hit in the UK.

works.title: (Shake Shake Shake), Shake Your Body
works.artist: went to No.1 on the US singles chart

description: KC and the Sunshine Band went to No.1 on the US singles chart with '(Shake Shake Shake), Shake Your Body', the group's third US No.1, a No.22 hit in the UK.
Donny Osmond started a three week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Go Away Little Girl'. The singers only US solo chart topper. The song had also been a No.1 for Steve Lawrence in 1963.

After George Martin insisted that session drummer Andy White took Ringo Starr's place, The Beatles returned to EMI Studios in London for a third attempt at recording their first single. 'Love Me Do' was selected to be The Beatles' first A-side, with "P.S. I Love You" on the flip side (a reversal of the original plan). The single that was released on October 5th featured a version of ‘Love Me Do’ with Ringo on drums, but the album ‘Please Please Me’ included a version with Andy White on drums.

American country music singer-songwriter and founding member of Lady Antebellum, Charles Kelley. Their debut album included the trio's debut hit, 'Love Don't Live Here', along with the singles, 'Lookin' for a Good Time' and 'I Run to You'.

American rapper and actor Ludacris, (Chris Bridges). He had the 2001 UK No.10 single with Missy Elliott, 'One Minute Man' and the 2002 US No.3 album Word Of Mouf. Outside of music, he has portrayed the character Tej Parker in the Fast & Furious film series.

Jonny Buckland, guitarist with Coldplay who had the 2000 UK No.4 single 'Yellow' and the 2000 UK No.1 album Parachutes and the 2005 worldwide No.1 album X&Y. The band have won a number of music awards throughout their career, including eight Brit Awards, winning Best British Group three times, five MTV Video Music Awards and seven Grammy Awards.

Singer, songwriter Richard Ashcroft, from English rock band The Verve, who had the 1997 album Urban Hymns, one of the best-selling albums in UK Chart history. The album features the hit singles 'Bitter Sweet Symphony', 'The Drugs Don't Work' and 'Lucky Man' and spent over 100 weeks on the UK chart. Ashcroft had the 2000 solo UK No.3 single 'A Song For The Lovers', and the 2000 UK No.1 album Alone With Everybody.
Gregory Kane, from the Scottish pop duo Hue and Cry. They had the 1987 UK No.6 single 'Labour Of Love'.

Moby, (Richard Hall), producer, vocalist, 1991 UK No.10 single 'Go'. His album Play was the biggest-selling UK indie album of 2000, spending 81 weeks on the chart and going platinum in over 20 countries. Moby is a descendant of 'Moby Dick' author Herman Melville. In addition to his music career, Moby is recognised for his veganism and advocacy for animal rights and humanitarian causes.

English keyboardist Mick Talbot. He was a co-founder of the Style Council with Paul Weller, and has also been a member of Dexys Midnight Runners, the Merton Parkas and the Bureau. With the Style Council, he had the 1983 UK No.3 single 'Long Hot Summer' plus 14 other UK Top 40 singles. In 2014, Talbot worked with Wilko Johnson and Roger Daltrey on the collaborative studio album Going Back Home.

English drummer Jon Moss from Culture Club, who had the 1983 UK No.1 & 1984 US No.1 single 'Karma Chameleon', plus seven other UK top 10 singles. He has also played with other bands, including London, the Nips, the Damned and Adam and the Ants.

American musician, singer, and songwriter Tommy Shaw from Styx who had the 1979 US No.1 & 1980 UK No.6 single 'Babe'. He has played with other groups including Damn Yankees and Shaw Blades as well as releasing several solo albums.
Dennis Tufano, lead singer with American Sunshine pop group The Buckinghams who had the 1967 US No.1 single 'Kind Of A Drag' and became one of the top selling US acts of 1967.

American percussionist and musicologist Mickey Hart, best known as one of the two drummers of the rock band Grateful Dead. In 1991, Hart produced the album Planet Drum, which remained at No.1 on the Billboard World Music chart for 26 weeks, and received the first ever Grammy Award for Best World Music Album.

American guitarist and singer, Jack Ely, best known for singing the Kingsmen's version of 'Louie Louie'. For a while, the record was banned by a handful of US radio stations because of its indecipherable lyrics, which were rumored to contain some naughty words. Even the F.B.I. investigated the song, but finally concluded that they could find nothing wrong. Ely died on 27th April 2015.

Bernie Dwyer, from the British 1960s pop band Freddie and the Dreamers. They scored the 1963 UK No.3 single 'You Were Made For Me', and the 1965 US No.1 single 'I'm Telling You Now'. Formed in 1962 in Manchester, the band was grouped as part of the Merseybeat sound phenomenon centred around Liverpool.

Taylor Swift was at No.1 on the US chart with her eighth studio album Folklore. The album had over 80.6 million global streams on Spotify and earned the Guinness World Record for the most opening-day streams for an album by a female artist. The album broke the Apple Music record for the most-streamed pop album in a day and the Amazon Music indie/alternative record. Folklore and its songs received five Grammy Award nominations at the 63rd ceremony, winning the Album of the Year.

Mark Ronson was being sued for alleged copyright infringement over his hit 2014 song Uptown Funk. Lastrada Entertainment, which owned the rights to the Roger and Zapp 1980 funk classic 'More Bounce To The Ounce', filed the lawsuit against the English producer claiming 'Uptown Funk' copied the first 48 seconds of 'More Bounce To The Ounce'.

US singer songwriter Johnny Cash died of respiratory failure aged 71. One of the most influential musicians of the 20th century, he was known as "The Man in Black." He traditionally started his concerts by saying, "Hello, I'm Johnny Cash." He had the 1969 US No.2 & UK No.4 single 'A Boy Named Sue', plus 11 other US Top 40 singles. Cash also had his own US TV show in the late 60s and early 70s. He released nearly 100 albums and more than 150 singles, and Cash experienced a late-career renaissance, thanks to his minimal and moving covers of songs like Nine Inch Nails’ 'Hurt' and Soundgarden’s 'Rusty Cage.' One of the best-selling artists in the history of popular music, Cash was an inductee of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, the Country Hall of Fame, and Gospel Hall of Fame.

The Vengaboys went to No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'We're Going To Ibiza!' The song was originally known as 'Barbados' a No.1 for Typically Tropical in 1975. The Vengaboys gave it a new title with revised lyrics.

Aerosmith released 'Pump' their tenth studio album which featured the hit singles: 'Love In An Elevator', 'The Other Side' and 'Janie's Got a Gun'. Aerosmith found themselves in law school textbooks after a small rock band named Pump sued Aerosmith's management company for service mark infringement. Aerosmith won the case.

Smokey Robinson and The Miracles were at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'The Tears Of A Clown', their first UK No.1. Stevie Wonder (who was discovered by Miracles member Ronnie White), and his producer Hank Cosby wrote the music for the song.

The Beatles were at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'She Loves You', the group's second No.1. The single set and surpassed several sales records in the United Kingdom charts, and set a record in the United States as one of the five Beatles songs that held the top five positions in the charts simultaneously, on 4 April 1964. It remains the band's best-selling single in the UK and was the top-selling single of the 1960s there by any artist.

The first 'teen idol', Frank Sinatra was at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Three Coins In The Fountain,' the singer's first UK No.1. The song was The Academy Award winning Best Original Song of 1954.

RM (Kim Nam-joon), South Korean singer, songwriter, with the boy band BTS. They became the first Korean act to top the US Billboard chart with their studio album Love Yourself: Tear (2018). BTS also became the fastest group since The Beatles to earn four US No.1 albums, doing so in less than two years. They became the first Asian act to chart a No.1 song in the US since Kyu Sakamoto with ‘Sukiyaki’ (1963).

Michael Paget, musician, singer, songwriter, and guitarist in the Welsh metalcore band Bullet for My Valentine. Their second album Scream Aim Fire peaked at No.2 on the UK chart and US Rock chart in 2008.
Jennifer Nettles, American Grammy-winning country music artist, lead vocalist with the duo Sugarland who had the 2009 US No.1 album Live on the Inside.
English soul singer Kenny Thomas, who had the 1991 UK No.4 single 'Thinking About Your Love'. Thomas's debut album Voices (1991) reached No.3 on the UK Albums Chart.

Jon Stewart, guitarist from English Britpop band Sleeper, who scored the 1996 UK No.10 single 'Sale Of The Century'. The group had eight UK top 40 hit singles and three UK top 10 albums during the 1990s. Their music was also featured in the soundtrack of the pop culture hit movie Trainspotting.

American singer-songwriter Ben Folds. He came to prominence as the frontman and pianist of the alternative rock trio Ben Folds Five from 1993 to 2000. Their single 'Brick' from the 1997 album Whatever and Ever Amen gained airplay on many mainstream radio stations. Folds went on to pursue a successful solo career.

Barry Andrews, keyboards with the English rock band XTC. The single 'Making Plans for Nigel' (1979) marked their commercial breakthrough, and in 1982 they had the UK No.10 single 'Senses Working Overtime'. Between 1979 and 1992, XTC had a total of 10 albums and 6 singles that reached the UK top 40. Andrews was also a co-founder of Shriekback and a member of the League of Gentlemen formed by King Crimson guitarist Robert Fripp.

American singer, songwriter, and musician Gerry Beckley. He was a founding member of the band America, who had the 1972 US No.1 and UK No.3 single 'Horse With No Name'. Their second album, Homecoming (1972), included the hit single 'Ventura Highway'.

works.title: Can't Get Enough of Your Love, Babe
You're the First, the Last, My Everything

description: American singer and songwriter Barry White. His greatest success came in the 1970s as a solo singer and with the Love Unlimited Orchestra, crafting many enduring R&B, soul, and disco songs such as his two biggest hits: 'Can't Get Enough of Your Love, Babe' and 'You're the First, the Last, My Everything'. White had 20 gold and 10 platinum singles, with worldwide record sales in excess of 100 million records. White was jailed for four months at the age of 16 for stealing $30,000 worth of Cadillac tyres. He died from Kidney failure on 4th July 2003, aged 58.

Colin Young, from British soul band The Foundations who scored the 1967 UK No.1 single 'Baby Now That I've Found You' and the 1969 US No.3 single 'Build Me Up A Buttercup'. The group was the first multi-racial group to have a No.1 hit in the UK in the 1960s.

American folk and blues singer Maria Muldaur, who had the 1974 US No.6 & UK No.21 single 'Midnight At The Oasis'. The song was nominated for both Record of the Year and Song of the Year at the 17th Annual Grammy Awards.

works.title: The Witch Queen Of New Orleans

description: Tony Bellamy, Redbone, who had the 1971 UK No.2 & US No.21 single 'The Witch Queen Of New Orleans' and the 1974 US No. 4 hit single, 'Come and Get Your Love.' Redbone are accredited in the NY Smithsonian as the first Native American rock/Cajun group to have a No.1 single in the United States and internationally. He died on December 25, 2009 of liver failure.

Kenyan/British singer-songwriter and musician Roger Whittaker died at a hospital near Toulouse, France aged 87. He scored the 1969 UK No.12 single 'Durham Town', and the 1975 UK No.2 & US No.19 single The Last Farewell which went to No.1 in 11 countries including the US and is one of the Best Selling Singles of all time. He was best known for his baritone singing voice and trademark whistling ability.

American singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Eddie Money died of cancer age 70. He released over ten albums and had a string of hits in the late Seventies including 'Baby Hold On', 'Two Tickets to Paradise' and 'Take Me Home Tonight'.

works.title: We'll Meet Again: The Very Best of Vera Lynn

description: Vera Lynn went to No.1 on the UK album chart with 'We'll Meet Again: The Very Best of Vera Lynn'. At the age of 92 it made her the oldest living artist to achieve this feat with an album. The previous oldest living artist to top the charts was Bob Dylan, who at 67 saw his album 'Together Through Life' become number one in the UK earlier this year.
The Verve scored their first and only UK No.1 single with 'The Drugs Don't Work', taken from their third album, Urban Hymns. The track became the band's most successful single in the United Kingdom.
Geffen Records threw a party to launch Nirvana's single 'Smells Like Teen Spirit'. The band ended up being thrown out of their own party after starting a food fight.
Michael Jackson started a five-week run at No.1 on the UK album chart with 'Bad', his follow up to the Thriller album It stayed at No.1 on the US chart for six weeks.
The Communards were at No.1 on the UK with the singles chart with 'Don't Leave Me This Way', which had been a hit for Harold Melvin & the Blue Notes in 1975 and later a hit for Thelma Houston.

Berlin went to No.1 on the US singles chart with the Giorgio Moroder written and produced 'Take My Breath Away'. On the B side, The Righteous Brothers 'You've Lost That Lovin' Feelin', both songs were featured in the film 'Top Gun'.

The Paul McCartney song 'Yesterday' was released as a Beatles single in the US. McCartney's vocal and acoustic guitar together with a string quartet essentially made for the first solo performance of the band. The final recording was so different from other works by The Beatles that the band members vetoed the release of the song as a single in the United Kingdom. (However, it was issued as a single there in 1976.)

A campaign was started in the UK to ban the American hit 'Tell Laura I Love Her' by Ray Peterson. The song was being denounced in the press as likely to inspire a teen-age "glorious death cult." The story told of a lovesick youngster who drives in a stock car race to win the hand of his sweetheart. He crashes and just before dying, groans out the words of the title.

works.title: What Makes You Beautiful
works.artist: One Direction who formed after finishing third in

description: Niall Horan, from English-Irish pop boy band One Direction who formed after finishing third in the seventh series of The X Factor in 2010. Scored the 2011 UK No.1 single 'What Makes You Beautiful' and the 2013 No.1 'One Way or Another (Teenage Kicks)'.
Brent Kutzle, bass guitar and cello with OneRepublic. Had the 2013 UK No.1 hit 'Counting Stars'.
Fiona Apple, US singer, songwriter, (1996 album 'Tidal').

American heavy metal singe Tim "Ripper' Owens. He first gained attention as the lead singer of Judas Priest, (replacing Rob Halford) and then Iced Earth. He took the nickname "Ripper" from the Judas Priest song 'The Ripper' during his time in the tribute band British Steel.

Randy Jones, from the American disco group The Village People. They had the hit singles 'Macho Man', 'In the Navy', 'Go West and the 1978 US No.2 hit Y.M.C.A. Its members were a symbolic group of fantasy stereotypes in attire often worn by gay men of Greenwich Village.

American musician, record producer and record executive Don Was, of the 1980s pop group group Was Not Was, who had the 1992 UK No.4 single 'Shake Your Head'. Was has worked with many artists including Iggy Pop, The B-52s, Jackson Browne, The Rolling Stones, Kris Kristofferson and John Mayer.

American singer Peter Cetera who with Chicago had the 1976 US & UK No.1 single 'If You Leave Me Now'. Cetera left the band in July 1985 and scored the solo 1986 US No.1 & UK No.3 single 'Glory Of Love' the theme song from the film The Karate Kid Part II.

Ray Elliot, keyboards, saxophone and flute with the Northern Irish band Them who had the 1965 UK hits 'Baby, Please Don't Go' and 'Here Comes The Night' with Van Morrison on lead vocals. Morrison quit the band in 1966 and went on to a successful career as a solo artist.

works.title: You've Made Me So Very Happy

description: David Clayton-Thomas, from jazz-rock American music group Blood Sweat & Tears. They scored the 1969 US No.2 single 'Spinning Wheel', and the 1969 US No.12 single 'You've Made Me So Very Happy'. They had a US No.1 with their second album Blood, Sweat & Tears in 1968.

Jamaican-British soul singer Jimmy James. Known for songs like 'Come to Me Softly', 'Now Is the Time' and 'I'll Go Where Your Music Takes Me' he performed as the lead singer of Jimmy James and the Vagabonds from the mid-1960s. He died on 14 May 2024, at the age of 83.
Kings Of Leon started a three week run at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Sex On Fire' taken from the band's fourth studio album Only by the Night.

Peter Andre scored his first UK No.1 single when 'Flava' went to the top for one week. The English-born Australian singer became a major television personality after taking part in the British reality TV series I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here!; during which he met and subsequently married glamour model Jordan. The couple split in May 2009 after three and a half years of marriage.
The lyrics to The Beatles song 'Getting Better' hand-written by Paul McCartney sold for £161,000 at a Sotheby's auction in London.
Cuban bandleader and composer Perez Prado died of a stroke in Mexico City. Had the US & UK 1955 No.1 single 'Cherry Pink & Apple Blossom White'.

The film Quadrophenia was released. Based on The Who's 1973 rock opera, the film featured Phil Daniels, Toyah Willcox, Ray Winstone, Michael Elphick and Sting. Unlike the adaptation of the Who album Tommy, Quadrophenia is not a musical, and the band does not appear.

Stevie Wonder started a two-week run at No.1 on the US album chart with his seventeenth studio album Fulfillingness First Finale, his second US No.1. The album received three Grammy Awards, including Album of the Year, in 1974. It is the fourth of five albums from what is considered Wonder's "classic period".

Eric Clapton scored a US No.1 with his version of the Bob Marley song I Shot the Sheriff which was first released in 1973 on The Wailers' album Burnin'. Clapton's version was included on his 1974 album 461 Ocean Boulevard.

The first episode of the comic strip 'The Archies' was aired on US TV. The recording group had contributions from Ron Dante, Andy Kim, Jeff Barry and others. Rock mogul, Don Kirshner (who also brought us The Monkees) was put in charge of the studio group. The following year The Archies started a eight-week run at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Sugar Sugar,' becoming the longest running One Hit Wonder in the UK.

American singer and songwriter Muni Long. Her debut studio album Jukebox was released in 2009. She then spent the following decade co-writing songs for other artists, including the hit singles 'Promise This' for Cheryl, 'California King Bed' for Rihanna, 'Worth It' for Fifth Harmony, 'Imagine' for Ariana Grande and the global hit 'Timber' for Pitbull.

Ghanaian rapper, singer, songwriter, Tinchy Stryder. He appeared in 2000 on pirate radio along with Dizzee Rascal and was part of grime collective and record production team Ruff Sqwad from 2001. He scored the 2009 UK No.2 album Catch 22 and the 2009 UK No.1 single 'Number 1' featuring N-Dub.

Amy Winehouse, UK singer, songwriter. Winehouse's debut album, Frank (2003), was a critical success in the UK and was nominated for the Mercury Prize. Her follow-up album, Back to Black (2006), led to five 2008 Grammy Awards, tying the then record for the most wins by a female artist in a single night, and made her the first British female to win five Grammys. Winehouse died of alcohol poisoning on 23 July 2011, aged 27. Her album Back to Black posthumously became, for a time, the UK's best-selling album of the 21st century.
Nas, (Nasir Jones), US rapper, (1996 UK No.12 single 'If I Ruled The World', 2007 US No.1 album 'Hip Hop Is Dead').

Mark Webber, from English rock band Pulp, who had the 1995 UK No.2 single 'Common People'. He quit the band in January 1997. Pulp were regarded among the Britpop "big four", along with Oasis, Blur and Suede.
John Power, singer, songwriter with The La's who had the 1990 UK No.13 single 'There She Goes'. As a member of Cast he had the 1996 UK No.4 single 'Flying'.

works.title: The Sun Always Shines On TV
Take On Me
works.artist: to score a UK and US No.1 hit

description: Norwegian singer Morten Harket who is the lead vocalist of the synth-pop band A-Ha. They scored the 1985 US No.1 single 'Take On Me' and the 1986 UK No.1 single 'The Sun Always Shines On TV', becoming the first Norwegian group to score a UK and US No.1 hit. 'Take On Me' was bolstered by the wide exposure on MTV of director Steve Barron's innovative music video featuring the band in a live-action pencil-sketch animation sequence. The video won six awards and was nominated for two others at the 1986 MTV Video Music Awards. On 17 February 2020, the music video for 'Take On Me' reached one billion views on YouTube. Harket was named a Knight First Class of the Order of St. Olav by King Harald for his services to Norwegian music and his international success.

American saxophonist and keyboardist Steve Berlin from Los Lobos (Spanish for "the Wolves"), who had the 1987 UK & US No.1 single with their cover version of 'La Bamba', which was a 1958 hit for Ritchie Valens and one of early rock and roll's best-known songs.

works.title: The Rain, The Park & Other Things

description: Barry Cowsill, from American singing group The Cowsills, who had the 1967 US No.2 single 'The Rain, The Park & Other Things', and the 1969 US No.2 single the theme from 'Hair'. TV's Partridge Family was based on The Cowsills family. He died from injuries caused by Hurricane Katrina in 2005. His body was not recovered until December 28th, 2005, from the Chartres Street Wharf, New Orleans. He was 51.
Paul Kossoff, guitar, Free (1970 UK No.2 & US No.4 single 'All Right Now'). Formed Back Street Crawler. Kossoff died of a heart attack on 19th March 1976 during a flight from Los Angeles to New York.

American musicia Steve Gaines, guitarist with Lynyrd Skynyrd who had the 1974 US No. 8 single 'Sweet Home Alabama' and the 1982 UK No.21 single 'Freebird'. Gaines was killed in a plane crash on 20th October 1977. The plane carrying the band between shows from Greenville, South Carolina to Baton Rouge, Louisiana, crashed outside of Gillsburg, Mississippi. Gaines died from blunt-force trauma to the head; he was 28 years old. The crash also killed Ronnie Van Zant, Steve's sister Cassie Gaines from the band.
Pete Agnew, from Scottish hard rock band Nazareth, who had the 1973 UK No.9 single 'Broken Down Angel', and the 1976 US No.8 single, 'Love Hurts'.

American vocalist Ivory Tilmon. He came to prominence in the vocal harmony group, The Detroit Emeralds. They enjoyed a run of successful records including their 1973 transatlantic hit single, 'Feel the Need in Me'. He died the day before his 73rd birthday on 13 Sept 2014.

English singer-songwriter and musician Tony Hooper. He was best known as a founder-member of Strawbs together with Dave Cousins. They are best known for their hit 'Part of the Union', which reached No.2 in the UK in 1973. He died on 18 Nov 2020 aged 81.

Songwriter Mae Boren Axton, known as the 'Queen Mother of Nashville' she wrote over 200 songs including a co-writing credit on the Elvis Presley hit 'Heartbreak Hotel'. She died on April 9th 1997 aged 82 after drowning in her bath at her home in Hendersonville, Tennessee after an apparent heart attack.

Donald Trump was found liable to pay damages to London singer and songwriter Eddy Grant for using his song 'Electric Avenue' without permission. It had taken Grant more than four years to sue the Republican candidate in this year’s presidential election in the US courts, over his 2020 campaign video that used a 40-second clip of the song. A federal judge in Manhattan ruled Mr Trump breached Mr Grant's copyright for his 1983 hit, and was now liable for damages as well as paying for the singer's legal fees.

Scottish drummer Kenny Hyslop died from prostate cancer at the age of 73. As a member of Scottish glam rock group Slik (with singer and guitarist Midge Ure), he had the 1976 UK No.1 single 'Forever And Ever'. Also a member of Skids who had the 1979 UK No.10 single 'Into The Valley' and he later joined Simple Minds and contributed to the recording of 'Promised You a Miracle'.

works.title: I Want You Back
works.artist: to debut with four consecutive No.1 hits on

works.title: Shake Your Body (Down to the Ground)
works.artist: to debut with four consecutive No.1 hits on

description: Tito Jackson, from the American family music group The Jackson 5 died of a heart attack in Gallup, New Mexico at the age of 70. The Jackson 5 were the first group to debut with four consecutive No.1 hits on the Hot 100 with the songs 'I Want You Back', 'ABC', 'The Love You Save', and 'I'll Be There'. And with The Jacksons, had the 1979 hit 'Shake Your Body (Down to the Ground)'. Jackson was on a road trip with his business partner Terry Harvey to transport Jackson's antique cars from California to his new residence in Claremore, Oklahoma when he began sweating and complaining of chest pains.

Ric Ocasek the former lead singer with The Cars was found dead in his New York City apartment, he was 75. The Cars formed in Boston in the mid-1970s by Ocasek and band-mate Benjamin Orr after they met at high school. Their early hits included 'Just What I Needed', 'My Best Friend's Girl' and 'Good Times Roll'. Their 1984 ballad 'Drive' was used as background music for footage of the Ethiopian famine, and its re-release as a single after Live Aid helped raise money for the cause. After the band broke up in the late 1980s, Ocasek embarked on a solo career as well as working as a producer for artists including Weezer, Bad Religion and No Doubt.

Pink Floyd keyboard player and founder member Richard Wright died aged 65 from cancer. Wright appeared on the group's first album, The Piper at the Gates of Dawn, in 1967 alongside Syd Barrett, Roger Waters and Nick Mason. David Gilmour who joined the band at the start of 1968 said: "He was such a lovely, gentle, genuine man and will be missed terribly by so many who loved him." In 2005, the full band reunited - for the first time in 24 years - for the Live 8 concert in London's Hyde Park. Wright had also contributed vocals and keyboards to Gilmour's 2006 solo album On An Island.

The Small Faces were at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'All Or Nothing', their only No.1 hit. According to Kay Marriott, Steve Marriott's mother, Steve wrote the song about his split with ex-fiancee Sue Oliver, though first wife Jenny Rylance states that Marriott told her he wrote the song for her as a result of her split with Rod Stewart.

Otis Redding released his third studio album Otis Blue. The album mainly consists of cover songs by popular R&B and soul artists and, bar one track, was recorded in a 24-hour period over July 9/10 1965 at the Stax Recording Studios in Memphis, Tennessee. In addition to topping the R&B Albums chart and landing at No.6 in the UK, the album produced three Top 40 hits, including 'Respect' (later popularised by Aretha Franklin), 'I’ve Been Loving You Too Long,' and a cover of The Rolling Stones’ '(I Can’t Get No) Satisfaction.' Today, Otis Blue is considered to be a definitive title in the soul canon and has been ranked as one of the greatest albums of all time by a variety of outlets, including Rolling Stone.
The Four Seasons started a five week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Sherry', it made No.8 in the UK. They became the first American group to have three No.1's in succession.

works.title: Surfin
works.artist: would re-record the song in October

description: A group from Hawthorne, California, called The Pendletones attend their first real recording session at Hite Morgan's studio in Los Angeles to record a demo called 'Surfin''. The Southern California group would re-record the song in October and, by the end of the year, they would sign their first record deal and be rechristened The Beach Boys. 'Surfin’', meanwhile, became their first single. It not only became a popular regional hit, but also broke into the Billboard Hot 100, peaking at No.75.

Elvis Presley started a five-week run at No.1 on the US charts with 'Don't Be Cruel'. The track went on to become Presley's biggest selling single, with sales over six million by 1961. This "double-sided hit" which had 'Hound Dog' on the B side, became the most successful on Billboard’s Hot 100 chart. One side reached No.1 on the chart, the other No.2. The two titles spent a combined 55 weeks in the Top 100 in 1956-1957.

works.title: Get Over Yourself
works.artist: who were created on the American television series

description: Ivette Sosa, singer from Eden's Crush, the American girl group who were created on the American television series Popstars who scored the 2001 Canadian No.1 and US No. 8 single 'Get Over Yourself'.

works.title: I've Got A Little Something For You

description: KG from British R&B-pop group MN8, who had the 1995 UK No.2 single 'I've Got A Little Something For You'.

works.title: Mmm Mmm Mmm Mmm
works.artist: Crash Test Dummies best known internationally for their

description: Michel Dorge drummer with Canadian rock band Crash Test Dummies best known internationally for their 1993 single 'Mmm Mmm Mmm Mmm'.
Tim Whelan, from British new wave band Furniture, who had the 1986 UK No.21 single 'Brilliant Mind'.

works.title: Could It Be I'm Falling In Love

description: British singer-songwriter Jaki Graham, who had the 1985 UK No.5 single 'Could It Be I'm Falling In Love'. In 1994, her cover version of Chaka Khan's hit 'Ain't Nobody' reached No.1 on the US Billboard Dance Club Songs.

Scottish singer Maggie Reilly, best known for her collaborations with the composer and instrumentalist Mike Oldfield. Most notably, she performed lead vocals on the Oldfield songs 'Family Man', 'Moonlight Shadow', 'To France', and 'Foreign Affair', all of which were international hits in the early 1980s.

Les Braid, bassist, from British Merseybeat band The Swinging Blue Jeans, who had the 1964 UK No.2 single 'Hippy Hippy Shake' and a cover of 'You're No Good', (later a 1974 US No.1 hit for Linda Ronstadt. Braid died on 31st July 2005.

American singer Signe Toly Anderson who was one of the founding members of the American rock band Jefferson Airplane. She sang on the first Jefferson Airplane album, Jefferson Airplane Takes Off, most notably on the song 'Chauffeur Blues'. She died on 28 January 2016.

American songwriter and record producer Sylvia Moyformerly, the first woman at the Detroit-based music label to write and produce for Motown acts. She is probably best known for her songs written with and for Stevie Wonder including 'Uptight (Everything's Alright)' and My 'Cherie Amour'. Moy died age 78 of complications from pneumonia on April 15, 2017.

American songwriter, performer, and writer Billy Edd Wheeler died at the age of 91. His songs include 'Jackson' (Grammy Award winner for Johnny Cash and June Carter), 'Coward of the County, ' a hit for Kenny Rogers (which inspired a 1981 television movie of the same name) and have been performed by over 160 artists and 'It’s Midnight' recorded by Elvis Presley.

Robbie Williams overtook Elvis Presley (13 No.1s), to become the solo artist with the most UK No.1 albums ever when his latest album XXV topped the UK chart. Only The Beatles had more UK No.1 albums than Robbie with 15 across their career.

Jackie Lomax died at his home in England aged 69. He first gained notice as the vocalist and bass player with The Undertakers, which were part of the Mersey Beat movement. He was later one of the first artists to sign with The Beatles label, Apple, with George Harrison penning his single 'Sour Milk Sea'.

works.title: I Heard It Through the Grapevine

description: Norman Whitfield died in Los Angeles, California from diabetes and other illnesses. The Motown songwriter and producer collaborated with Barrett Strong on such hits as 'I Heard It Through the Grapevine', ‘Ain't Too Proud to Beg’, ‘(I Know) I'm Losing You’, ‘Cloud Nine’, ‘War’, ‘Papa Was a Rolling Stone’, and ‘Car Wash’.
Austrian act DJ Otzi went to No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Hey Baby', a Euro-dance version of Bruce Channel's No.2 hit from 1962.

Kate Bush released her fifth studio album Hounds of Love. The album's lead single, 'Running Up That Hill', became one of Bush's biggest hits and the album produced three further successful singles, 'Cloudbusting', 'Hounds of Love', and 'The Big Sky'. NME placed Hounds of Love 48th on their "500 Greatest Albums of All-Time" list. In 2022, after it was featured in the Netflix series Stranger Things, 'Running Up That Hill' reached No.1 in eight countries, including the UK, and No.3 on the US chart. In 2023, it reached a billion streams on Spotify.

The Sugarhill Gang introduced the world to hip-hop with their single 'Rapper’s Delight.' Opening with the now-classic lyric "I said a hip hop the hippie to the hippie/ To the hip hip hop and you don’t stop," the track riffs off the upbeat bassline of Chic’s 'Good Times' and features the dextrous wordplay of Michael "Wonder Mike" Wright, Henry "Big Bank Hank" Jackson, and Guy "Master Gee" O’Brien. While the track wasn’t the first instance of rap on record, it was the first single to popularise the genre on a global level, landing in the US Top 40 and in the Top Ten in the UK, Canada, and across Europe. It has since been added to the Library of Congress’s National Recording Registry.

Johnny Cash was at No.1 on the Billboard Country singles chart with 'A Boy Named Sue'. The song tells the tale of a young man's quest for revenge on a father who abandoned him at 3 years of age and whose only contribution to his entire life was naming him Sue, commonly a feminine name, which results in the young man suffering from ridicule and harassment by everyone he meets in his travels.

'She Loves You' by The Beatles was released by Swan Records in the US. Although the song was currently No.1 in the UK, 'She Loves You' was ignored in the US until 1964 when it would reach the top of the US Pop chart.
Anne Shelton was at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Lay Down Your Arms.' Shelton was a British vocal star of the 40s & 50s and one time singer with the Glenn Miller Orchestra.

Nick Jonas, from American pop rock band Jonas Brothers, who had the 2009 US No.1 album Lines, Vines and Trying Times. They gained popularity from their appearances on Disney Channel. They starred in the 2008 Disney Channel Original Movie Camp Rock and its 2010 sequel, Camp Rock 2: The Final Jam. They also starred in their own Disney Channel series Jonas.
Katie Melua, UK singer, songwriter, (2004 UK No.1 album 'Call Off The Search', 2004 UK Top 10 single 'The Closest Thing To Crazy', 2007 UK No.1 single 'What a Wonderful World' with Eva Cassidy).
American R&B artist Musiq Soulchild, (born Talib Johnson) who had the 2007 US No.1 album Luvanmusiq, which spawned the single 'Halfcrazy', his highest entry at No. 16 on the Billboard Hot 100.

Tina Barrett from English pop group S Club 7 who had the 1999 UK No.1 single 'Bring It All Back'. Their 2000 UK No.1 album 7 spent over a year on the UK chart. The group was formed in 1998 and quickly rose to fame by starring in their own BBC television series, Miami 7.

American singer, songwriter, and actor Marc Anthony, who had the 2000 US No.2 single 'You Sang To Me'. He is the top-selling tropical salsa artist of all time, a four-time Grammy Award, eight-time Latin Grammy Award and twenty-nine-time Lo Nuestro Awards winner (the most of any male). Anthony, has sold more than 12 million albums worldwide.

American singer-songwriter Richard Marx. He is the only male artist in history to have his first seven singles reach the top 5 of the Billboard charts. He has scored a total of 14 No.1 singles, both as a performer and as a songwriter/producer. As a singer, his No. 1 hits include 'Hazard', 'Right Here Waiting', 'Hold On to the Nights', 'Endless Summer Nights', and 'Satisfied'. Marx has been nominated for five Grammy Awards. In 2003, he won the Grammy for Song of the Year for 'Dance with My Father'.
Stephen Jones, singer, guitarist, from British indie band Babybird, who had the 1996 UK No.3 single ‘You’re Gorgeous’, and the 1996 UK No.9 album Ugly Beautiful.

Alan Barton from Black Lace who had the 1984 UK No.2 single 'Agadoo'. The track earned them the dubious accolade of being voted as the worst song of all time by a panel of music writers for Q Magazine. Barton replaced Chris Norman in Smokie in 1986, recording six albums with them. He died on 23 March 1995 aged 41 from injuries incurred when Smokie's tour bus crashed during a hailstorm in Cologne, Germany.

American bassist Ron Blair from Tom Petty & The Heartbreakers who had the 1977 single 'American Girl', and the 1989 UK No.28 single 'I Won't Back Down' and the 1991 UK No.3 album Into The Great Wide Open. He was originally the band's bassist from 1976 to 1981. In 2002, he returned to the group after a 20-year hiatus, replacing his own replacement, the late Howie Epstein.
David Bellamy, Bellamy Brothers, (1976 US No.1 single 'Let Your Love Flow', 1979 UK No.3 single 'If I Said I Had A Beautiful Body Would You Hold It Against Me').

Kenny Jones, drummer, The Small Faces (1967 UK No.3 single 'Itchycoo Park' & 1968 UK No.1 album 'Ogden's Nut Gone Flake'). The Faces (1972 UK No.6 single 'Stay With Me'). The Who (after Keith Moon, 1981 UK No.9 single 'You Better You Bet').
American singer Betty Kelly from Martha And The Vandellas, (1964 US No.2 & 1969 UK No.4 single 'Dancing In The Street'). She was also a member of Motown singing group The Velvelettes.

Bernie Calvert, bassist with British pop/rock group The Hollies ( from 1966 until 1981), who have scored over 30 top 40 hits, including 'Just One Look', 'Bus Stop', 'Carrie Anne', and later He Ain’t Heavy He’s My Brother and 'The Air That I Breathe'.
American drummer, singer and actor Joe Butler, who with The Lovin Spoonful had the 1966 US No.1 & UK No.8 single 'Summer In The City'.

American singer, songwriter JD Souther died at the age of 78. He wrote and co-wrote songs recorded by Linda Ronstadt (Souther helped The Eagles to form as a backing band for Ronstadt) and some of the Eagles biggest hits, including 'Best of My Love', 'Victim of Love', 'Heartache Tonight' and 'New Kid in Town'. He recorded two hit songs in his solo career: 'You're Only Lonely' (1979) and 'Her Town Too' (1981), a duet with James Taylor. In 1972 he formed the Souther–Hillman–Furay Band with Chris Hillman of The Byrds and Richie Furay of Buffalo Springfield. He dated Linda Ronstadt and Stevie Nicks in the 1970s.
Adele went to No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Someone Like You'. The track was also No.1 in Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, Finland, France, Italy, Poland, Switzerland, the United Kingdom.
Justin Timberlake went to No.1 on the UK album chart with 'Futuresex / Lovesounds' the singers second solo album and second No.1.
English singer Frankie Vaughan died of heart failure aged 71. During the 1950s he scored twenty UK Top 30 singles including the UK No.2 'Green Door.' He was awarded an OBE in 1965, and a CBE in 1996

The video for Queen's single 'Bicycle Race' was filmed at Wimbledon Stadium, Wimbledon, UK. It featured 65 naked female professional models racing around the stadium's track on bicycles, which had been hired for the day. The rental company was reported to have requested payment for all the saddles when they found out how their bikes had been used. Directed by Denis de Vallance (who also directed visuals for The Pointer Sisters, The Clash, Kool & The Gang, and more), the concept involved them racing at the Wimbledon greyhound racing track.
Jonathan Jacob Walker, bassist, with American rock band Panic! at the Disco who scored the 2008 Australian No.1 and US & UK No.2 album Pretty.Odd.

works.title: Get Over Yourself
works.artist: who were created on the American television series

description: Maile Misajon, singer from Eden's Crush, the American girl group who were created on the American television series Popstars who scored the 2001 Canadian No.1 and US No. 8 single 'Get Over Yourself'.

Adam Devlin from English indie rock band The Bluetones. Their debut studio album, released in February 1996, knocked Oasis's (What's the Story) Morning Glory? off the No.1 spot in the UK Albums Chart for a week. The second single from their debut album 'Slight Return' peaked at No.2 on the UK Singles Chart. The song is named after the subtitle for 'Voodoo Child (Slight Return)' by Jimi Hendrix.

Keith Flint, vocals, with English electronic dance music group The Prodigy who scored the 1996 UK No.1 & US No. 30 single 'Firestarter' and the 1997 UK & US No.1 album 'The Fat Of The Land'. Flint died at his Essex home in England on 4 March 2019 age 49.

John Penney singer from English rock band Neds Atomic Dustbin, who had the 1991 UK No.16 single 'Happy'. Their debut album God Fodder (1991), made No. 4 in the UK albums chart. The band took their name from an episode of radio comedy programme The Goon Show.

American singer-songwriter, composer, and record producer Anastacia, who had the 2000 UK No. 6 single 'I'm Outta Love'. Her 2000 album Not That Kind spent 65 weeks on the UK album chart. Anastacia began her career in 1983 as a dancer. In 1990, she started her music career as a backing vocalist working with Jamie Foxx on his debut album Peep This, and later recorded with Paula Abdul.

Australian film director, producer, writer Baz Luhrmann, who scored the 1999 UK No.1 single 'Everybody's Free To Wear Sunscreen'. On the screen, he is best known for his Red Curtain Trilogy, consisting of his romantic comedy film Strictly Ballroom (1992) and the romantic tragedies William Shakespeare's Romeo + Juliet (1996) and Moulin Rouge! (2001).
William Owen Gregory, keyboards and synthesiser from the English electronic music duo Goldfrapp who had the 2008 UK No.2 album Seventh Tree.

Fee Waybill, lead singer and songwriter of San Francisco band The Tubes, known for their 1977 hit single 'White Punks On Dope' and the 1983 US No.10 single 'She's A Beauty'. Waybill has also worked with other acts, including Toto, Richard Marx, and Billy Sherwood.

Roger Nichols, American composer and songwriter, multi-instrumentalist. He co-wrote many songs including, 'We've Only Just Begun' (The Carpenters), which was originally written for a Crocker Bank commercial and 'Out in the Country' (Three Dog Night). He died from pneumonia at his home on 17 May 2025, at the age of 84.

American vocalist Lamonte McLemore, from The 5th Dimension. Between 1967 and 1973, they charted with 20 Top 40 hits on the Billboard Hot 100, two of which, 'Up, Up and Away' (No. 7, 1967) and the 1969 No. 1 'Medley: Aquarius/Let the Sunshine In (The Flesh Failures)' won the Grammy Award for Record of the Year.

American bassist Bill Black, who worked with Elvis Presley from 1954-1957 and later the Bill Black Combo. Black played on early Presley recordings including 'Good Rockin' Tonight', 'Heartbreak Hotel', 'Baby Let's Play House', 'Mystery Train', 'That's All Right', and 'Hound Dog', and eventually became one of the first bass players to use the Fender Precision Bass (bass guitar) in popular music, on 'Jailhouse Rock', in the late 1950s. After two surgeries and lengthy hospital stays, Black died of a brain tumor on 21 October 1965, at age 39. Black's main stand-up bass is today owned by Paul McCartney, who received the instrument as a birthday present from his wife Linda in the late 1970s.

American blues, rock and folk singer, songwriter, and guitarist Nick Gravenites died at the age of 85. He is best known for his work with Electric Flag (as their lead singer), Janis Joplin and Mike Bloomfield. He wrote several songs for Joplin, including 'Work Me, Lord' produced the pop hit 'One Toke Over the Line' for Brewer & Shipley and the album Right Place, Wrong Time for Otis Rush, for which he was nominated for a Grammy Award.

Australian bass guitarist Dick Diamonde died at the age of 76. He was a member of The Easybeats who are widely regarded as Australia's greatest pop group of the mid-1960s. They scored the 1966 Australian No.1, UK No.6 and 1967 US No.16 single 'Friday On My Mind', which was the first Australian rock song to achieve international success. Their concerts and public appearances were regularly marked by intense fan hysteria similar to "Beatlemania", soon dubbed "Easyfever" by the Australian press.

works.title: Best of My Love
works.artist: The Emotions died at the age of

description: Pamela Hutchinson from the American soul/R&B vocal group The Emotions died at the age of 61. The Emotions scored the 1977 US No. 1 hit 'Best of My Love'.

American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift was at no.1 on the US singles chart with 'Shake It Off', becoming Swift's second No.1 single in the United States and the 22nd song to debut at No.1 in the chart's history.

Leonard Cohen collapsed on stage during a concert in Valencia in Spain and was taken to hospital. He was later discharged after doctors told him he had food poisoning. Cohen was in the middle of singing his song 'Bird On The Wire' when he fainted, prompting the band to stop playing and rush to help him.
Garth Brooks went to No.1 on the US album chart with 'In Pieces'. The album spent 25 weeks on the chart and sold over 6m copies. The album peaked at No.2 on the UK chart.
The seven-minute epic by Dire Straits 'Private Investigations' went to No.2 on the UK singles chart, held off No.1 by survivors 'Eye Of The Tiger'.

The Eagles released 'Heartache Tonight' from their album The Long Run. The song originated from an jam session between Glenn Frey and J. D. Souther who would visit Frey's home in Los Angeles whenever he was in town on tour. Frey and Souther wrote the first verse while listening to Sam Cooke songs. In the heat of jamming, Frey called Bob Seger on the phone and sang him the verse. Seger then blurted out the chorus.

Japanese singer Joji (George Miller). His 2022 single 'Glimpse of Us' from his third studio album Smithereens became the second song by a Japanese artist to reach the top 10 on the US chart after Kyu Sakamoto's 'Sukiyaki' in 1963.

Danish-Irish singer, songwriter Lukas Forchhammer, the lead vocalist for the Danish band Lukas Graham who had the 2016 hit '7 Years' which topped the charts in Denmark, Sweden, Italy, Austria, Australia, New Zealand, Ireland, the UK and Canada.
American singer Ricky Bell, from American R&B group New Edition who had the 1983 UK No.1 single 'Candy Girl', and Bell Biv DeVoe who had the 1990 US No.3 single 'Do Me!'.
Ian Spice, drummer from English pop band Breathe who had the 1988 UK No.4 and US No.2 single 'Hands To Heaven'.

works.title: Good Enough
works.artist: rose to prominence during the Britpop era of

description: Nigel Clarke from English power pop rock trio Dodgy. The band rose to prominence during the Britpop era of the 1990s and had the 1996 UK No.4 single 'Good Enough', which was featured on the soundtrack to the 1998 movie Sliding Doors.

Mike Heaton, drummer, for the alternative rock band Embrace. The band's highest-charting single is 'Nature's Law', which reached No.2 on the UK Singles Chart in 2006. The albums This New Day, Out of Nothing and The Good Will Out all reached No.1 on the UK Albums Chart.

works.title: Dare
works.artist: attained widespread commercial success with their third album

works.title: Don't You Want Me
works.artist: attained widespread commercial success with their third album

description: Joanne Catherall, singer with The Human League. Formed in Sheffield, England in 1977 the group attained widespread commercial success with their third album Dare in 1981. The album contained four hit singles, including the UK/US No.1 hit 'Don't You Want Me'.

Richard Walmsley, from English electronic group Beatmasters, who had the 1988 UK No.5 single 'Rock Da House'. The Beatmasters went on to produce and remix records for other artists, including Pet Shop Boys, Erasure and Marc Almond.

works.title: I Just Died In Your Arms Tonight

description: Martin Beedle, drummer, with English rock band Cutting Crew, who scored the 1987 US No.1 & 1986 UK No.4 single 'I Just Died In Your Arms Tonight'.

American drummer Michael Hossack who as a member of The Doobie Brothers between 1971 and 1973, playing on several of the band's best-known hits, including 'Listen to the Music' and 'China Grove'. Hossack died of cancer on 12 March 2012 at his home in Dubois, Wyoming at the age of 65.

English guitarist and singer Alan King, best known for his time with the British 1960s pop group The Action and the 1970s rock band Ace, who scored the 1974 UK No.20 single 'How Long'. The song later reached No.3 on the US chart in the spring of 1975.

American singer, actor and former teen idol Frankie Avalon. He had 31 charting US Billboard singles from 1958 to late 1962, including No.1 hits, 'Venus' in 1959 and 'Why' in 1960. On his twenty-first birthday, Frankie Avalon was given $600,000 (£330,000) that he earned as a minor from his hit records. He had a supporting role in the 1978 musical film Grease, in which he sings the song 'Beauty School Dropout'.

American pop singer Jimmie Rodgers, who had a brief run of mainstream popularity in the 1950s and 1960s with a string of crossover singles, including the 1957 US No.1 single 'Honeycomb'. His biggest hit in the UK was 'English Country Garden', a version of the folk song 'Country Gardens', which reached No.5 in the chart in June 1962. Rodgers died from kidney disease on January 18, 2021, at the age of 87.

American singer and songwriter Sonny Curtis died from pneumonia at a hospital in Nashville, Tennessee, at the age of 88. He was a member of The Crickets, who had the 1957 US No.1 single 'That'll Be The Day' the 1959 UK No.1 single 'It Doesn't Matter Anymore' plus over 15 other UK Top 40 singles. He wrote 'Walk Right Back', which was a 1960 hit for the Everly Brothers, 'I Fought the Law', notably covered by the Bobby Fuller Four and the Clash. Later, Curtis wrote the theme song of The Mary Tyler Moore Show, 'Love Is All Around, which he also recorded for the show. The song was covered by Hüsker Dü in 1985, and by Joan Jett in 1996.

Ozzy Osbourne’s former drummer, Lee Kerslake, died aged 73 from prostate cancer. He is best known for his performances on the Black Sabbath frontman’s critically-acclaimed debut album, Blizzard of Ozz, and was also the drummer in Uriah Heep appearing on their 1972 album Demons and Wizards and nine studio records, as well as a live album, with the band before departing in 1978.

American musician, songwriter, and record producer, Ed Cobb died. He was a member of the Four Preps and he wrote the northern soul hit Tainted Love for Gloria Jones, (the B-side of her 1965 single 'My Bad Boy's Comin' Home') Soft Cell reworked the song into one of the biggest pop hits of the 1980s.

Robbie Williams scored his first solo UK No.1 single after leaving Take That with 'Millennium', taken from his second album, I've Been Expecting You. The song also became an international success; it managed to break into the Top 40 around the world. It also became Williams' first song to chart on the US Billboard Hot 100 when it was released in 1999.

Pearl Jam released their second studio album Vs. The album set the record for the most copies of an album sold in its first week, a record it held for five years, despite the fact that the group declined to produce music videos for any of the album’s singles.

Radiohead filmed the video for their new single 'Creep' during a show at the Venue, in Oxford, England. During its initial release, 'Creep' was not a chart success. However, upon re-release in 1993, it became a worldwide hit.

The Shamen started a four-week run at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Ebeneezer Goode'. One of the most controversial UK chart toppers due to its perceived subliminal endorsement of recreational drug use. The song was initially banned by the BBC.

The Rolling Stones album 'Tattoo You' started a nine-week run at No.1 on the US chart, the band's ninth US No.1. The group's sixteenth UK and eighteenth US studio album was mostly composed of studio outtakes recorded during the 1970s, and contains one of the band's best-known songs, 'Start Me Up', which hit No.2 on the US Billboard singles charts.

Diana Ross started a three-week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Ain't No Mountain High Enough'. The singers first solo No.1 since leaving The Supremes a No.6 in the UK. Written by American singers and songwriters Nickolas Ashford & Valerie Simpson in 1966 for the Tamla label. The song was first successful as a 1967 hit single recorded by Marvin Gaye and Tammi Terrell. Ross was nominated for the Grammy Award for Best Female Pop Vocal Performance for the song.

Creedence Clearwater Revival scored their only UK No.1 single with 'Bad Moon Rising' a US No.2 hit. Taken as the lead track from their Green River album, in the 1981 film An American Werewolf in London, 'Bad Moon Rising' plays as David nears the moment of changing into a werewolf. Green River.
Former chicken plucker Chubby Checker went to No.1 on the US singles chart with 'The Twist'. It made No.14 in the UK in 1962, version with The Fat Boys made No.2 in the UK in 1988.
Alan Jay "A. Jay" Popoff from the American rock pop punk band Lit. Best known for their 1999 album A Place in the Sun, which featured the hit single 'My Own Worst Enemy'.

Paul Winterhart, drummer with English psychedelic rock band Kula Shaker. Between 1996 and 1999, they had several Top 10 hits on the UK Singles Chart, including 'Tattva', 'Hey Dude', 'Govinda' and 'Hush'. The band's debut album, K, reached No. 1 on the UK Albums Chart.

American country singer Trisha Yearwood. Her 1991 debut single 'She's in Love with the Boy', became a No.1 hit on the Billboard country singles chart and her self-titled debut album sold over two million copies. Yearwood's 1997 single 'How Do I Live' reached No.2 on the US country singles chart and was internationally successful.

Jarvis Cocker, singer, from English rock band Pulp, who had the 1995 UK No.2 single 'Common People'. He quit the band in January 1997. Pulp were regarded among the Britpop "big four", along with Oasis, Blur and Suede. He later presented a BBC Radio 6 Music show called Jarvis Cocker's Sunday Service.

American guitarist, vocalist, and songwriter Lita Ford. She was a member of The Runaways and then embarked on a successful glam metal solo career that hit its peak in the late 1980s. The 1989 single 'Close My Eyes Forever, a duet with Ozzy Osbourne, remains Ford's most successful song, reaching No. 8 on the US Billboard Hot 100. (1989 UK No.47 single with Ozzy Osbourne 'Close My Eyes Forever').

British-Irish musician Rusty Egan, who, with The Rich Kids, had the 1978 UK No. 24 single 'Rich Kids', and later with Visage, the 1981 UK No. 8 single 'Fade To Grey'. He played drums on a remixed version of Phil Lynott's song 'Yellow Pearl', which the BBC used as the Top of the Pops theme tune from 1981 to 1986.

American musician, songwriter, guitarist and record producer Nile Rodgers. He was the lead guitarist and co-founding member (with Bernard Edwards) of the band Chic, who had the 1978 US No.1 & UK No.7 single 'Le Freak'. With Edwards, Rodgers wrote and produced music for other artists, including Diana Ross, Sister Sledge, David Bowie (Let's Dance album), INXS, Duran Duran and Madonna. Rodgers has also worked with many artists including Kylie Minogue, Jeff Beck, Avicii, Daft Punk, Mick Jagger, Coldplay, Grace Jones, Bryan Ferry, Christina Aguilera, Lady Gaga and Beyoncé.

Daniel Lanois, producer, singer. He produced the 1986 Peter Gabriel album, So, along with albums by Brian Eno, U2, (The Unforgettable Fire, Joshua Tree and Achtung Baby), (Bob Dylan, (Oh Mercy) Neil Young, Robbie Robertson, Emmylou Harris and Willie Nelson. Lanois released the 1990 solo album Acadie. Three albums produced or co-produced by Lanois have won the Grammy Award for Album of the Year.

English musician and music video director Lol Creme. With 10cc, he scored the UK No.1 & US No.2 single 'I'm Not In Love', plus 10 other UK Top 30 hits. From 1972 to 1978, 10cc had five consecutive UK top-ten albums: Sheet Music (1974), The Original Soundtrack (1975), How Dare You! (1976), Deceptive Bends (1977) and Bloody Tourists (1978). As one half of Godley & Creme, he had the 1981 UK No.3 single 'Under Your Thumb'. In 1988, Creme became a member of the band Art of Noise, with Anne Dudley and Trevor Horn.

John Coghlan drummer with English rock band Status Quo, (he left in 1982), who had the 1977 UK No.3 single 'Rockin' All Over The World'. Other hits include 'Pictures of Matchstick Men' in 1968, and 'Whatever You Want' in 1979.

American multi-instrumentalist, singer, and songwriter David Bromberg. He has played and recorded with many famous musicians, including Richie Havens, Jerry Jeff Walker, Willie Nelson, Jerry Garcia and Bob Dylan. He co-wrote the song 'The Holdup' with George Harrison, who played on Bromberg's self-titled 1972 album.
Freda Payne, US soul singer, who had the 1970 US No.3 & UK No.1 single 'Band Of Gold'. Payne is the older sister of Scherrie Payne, a former singer with The Supremes.

works.title: Dream a Little Dream of Me

description: Cass Elliott, singer, Mamas and the Papas, who scored the 1966 US No.1 & UK No.3 single 'Monday Monday'. After the breakup of The Mamas & the Papas, Elliot embarked on a solo career and had the 1968 hit 'Dream a Little Dream of Me' from her solo album of the same name. Elliott died from a heart attack on 29th July 1974 while staying at Harry Nilsson's London flat in the UK.

Mike Hurst from the British pop-folk vocal trio The Springfields who had the 1962 US No. 20 single 'Silver Threads And Golden Needles', and the 1963 UK No.5 single 'Island Of Dreams'. The Springfields included singer Dusty Springfield and her brother, record producer Tom Springfield.

American composer, singer, and songwriter Paul Williams. He wrote The Carpenters hits 'We've Only Just Begun' & 'Rainy Day's and Mondays', Three Dog Night's 'An Old Fashioned Love Song' and 'Out in the Country' and 'Evergreen (Love Theme from A Star Is Born)', a No. 1 hit for Barbra Streisand.

Lloyd Parks, American R&B/soul singer with Harold Melvin & The Blue Notes, (noted for his high tenor and falsetto vocal leads and harmonies). He is also a founding member of The Epsilons who backed Arthur Conley on his Atco Records 1967 hit single 'Sweet Soul Music'.

works.title: Sherry
works.artist: The Four Seasons who had the

works.title: December 1963, (Oh What A Night
works.artist: The Four Seasons who had the

description: Nick Massi from American rock and pop band The Four Seasons who had the 1960s hits 'Sherry', 'Big Girls Don't Cry', 'Walk Like a Man', and the 1976 UK & US No.1 single 'December 1963, (Oh What A Night'). They are one of the best-selling musical groups of all time, having sold an estimated 100 million records worldwide. Massi died on 24th December 2000.
Brook Benton, US singer, (1959 UK No.28 single 'Endlessly', 1979 US No.4 single 'Rainy Night In Georgia'). He died on 9th April 1998.

Ed Sheeran was at No.1 with his eighth studio album Play. It became Sheeran's ninth consecutive chart-topper in the United Kingdom. In the United States, Sheeran scored his eighth top 10-charting album on the Billboard 200.

works.title: Something About The Way You Look Tonight

description: Elton John started a six week run at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Something About The Way You Look Tonight', and 'Candle In The Wind 97.' A re-write of his 1974 hit about Marilyn Monroe. This version was raising funds for the Diana, Princess of Wales charity, following her death in Paris. It went on to become the biggest selling single in the world ever.

The Daily Mirror ran a front-page story 'Ban this sick stunt' referring to the new single from Pulp 'Sorted For E's & Wizz.' The artwork showed how to fold a 'speed' wrap, the sleeve was changed, and the single later entered the UK chart at No.8.

AC/DC released their third studio album 'Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap'. The album has been certified 6x Platinum in the United States, which means that it has sold at least 6 million copies, becoming the third highest sold album by AC/DC in the US after 'Highway To Hell' and 'Back In Black'.

works.title: Saturday Night
works.artist: scored the US No.1 hit with

description: Scottish group The Bay City Rollers made their US TV debut when they appeared on the Saturday Night Variety Show. The group scored the US No.1 hit with 'Saturday Night' when released in January 1976.

On his way to perform his second concert of the day, US singer, songwriter Jim Croce was killed with five others when his chartered aircraft hit a tree on take off in Louisiana. Croce's breakthrough came in 1972, when his third album, You Don't Mess Around with Jim, produced three charting singles, including 'Time in a Bottle', which reached No. 1 after Croce died.

The Rolling Stones live album 'Get Your Ya-Yas Out' started a two-week run at No.1 on the UK chart. Recorded at New York's Madison Sq Gardens on 27th & 28th Nov 1969, featuring 'Jumpin Jack Flash', 'Honky Tonk Woman' and 'Midnight Rambler'.

UK music paper Melody Maker readers poll results were published. Winners included Eric Clapton who won best musician, Bob Dylan best male singer and best album for 'Nashville Skyline'. Best group went to The Beatles, Best single went to Simon And Garfunkel for 'The Boxer' and Janis Joplin won Best female singer.

Buddy Holly released the single 'Peggy Sue' with 'Everyday' as the B-side. The song was originally entitled 'Cindy Lou', after Holly's niece, but was later changed to 'Peggy Sue' in reference to Peggy Sue Gerron the girlfriend (and future wife) of Jerry Allison, the drummer for the Crickets, after the couple had temporarily broken up.
Keith Semple, from British boy band One True Voice, created on the ITV television series Popstars: The Rivals who had the 2002 UK No.2 single 'Sacred Trust / After You're Gone'.
Rick Woolstenhulme, drummer with American rock band Lifehouse who had the 2001 US No.10 & UK No.25 single 'Hanging By A Moment' from their debut studio album, No Name Face.

American singer, songwriter, and record producer The-Dream. His co-writing credits include 'Me Against the Music' (2003) for Britney Spears, 'Umbrella' (2007) for Rihanna, 'Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)' (2008), for Beyoncé, 'Touch My Body' (2008) for Mariah Carey. His work has earned him eight Grammy Awards from 21 nominations, including an inaugural nomination for Songwriter of the Year at the 65th Annual Grammy Awards.

American musician Ben Shepherd best known as the bassist of the alternative rock band Soundgarden. Their 1994 single 'Black Hole Sun' topped the US Billboard Album Rock Tracks chart, where it spent a total of seven weeks at No.1. Soundgarden was the first grunge band to be signed to a major label when they signed to A&M Records in 1988.

works.title: Can't Live Without Your Love and Affection

description: Matthew and Gunnar Nelson, from the American hard rock duo Nelson. The twin sons of 60s singer Ricky Nelson scored the 1990 US No.1 single, 'Can't Live Without Your Love and Affection'. They are listed in the Guinness Book of World Records as the only family to reach No.1 record status in three successive generations (beginning with grandparents Ozzie and Harriet Nelson).

David Hemmingway who with The Housemartins had the 1986 UK No.1 single 'Caravan Of Love' and with The Beautiful South the 1990 UK No.1 single 'A Little Time' plus over fifteen other UK Top 40 singles.

Alannah Currie, lyricist, percussionist, visual stylist, and backing vocalist. With The Thompson Twins, she scored the 1984 UK No.2 single 'You Take Me Up' and the 1984 US No.3 single 'Hold Me Now'. Her songwriting credits also include 'I Want That Man', an international hit for Deborah Harry in 1989.

English-Australian rock guitarist Harvey James. He was a member of the bands Mississippi (1973–74), Ariel (1974–75), Sherbet (1976–80) who scored the No.1 hit 'Howzat' (1976). James died on 15 January 2011, aged 58.

Chuck and John Panozzo, American twin brothers who co-founded the rock band Styx. They are best known for their 1979 US No.1 & 1980 UK No.6 single 'Babe'. In 1981, Styx's Paradise Theatre was a No. 1 album in the US and Canada. John Panozzo died of gastrointestinal hemorrhaging and cirrhosis in Chicago on July 16, 1996.
American R&B singer Sweet Pea Atkinson from Was Not Was, who had the 1992 UK No.4 single 'Shake Your Head'. He died from a heart attack in Los Angeles, on 5 May 2020 aged 74.

Bobby Nunn, who was a member of The Robins and The Coasters who scored the 1958 US No.1 single 'Yakety Yak', the 1959 US No.2 and UK No.6 single 'Charlie Brown', as well as 'Young Blood' and 'Poison Ivy'. Nunn died on nov 5th 1986.

Swedish drummer Roger Palm died at the age of 75. Working as a session musician he appeared on such noteworthy ABBA songs as 'Mamma Mia', 'Dancing Queen', 'Thank You For The Music' and 'Take A Chance On Me'. During the 70s he was a member of Swedish bands the Gimmicks and then the Beatmakers, and started working on the session circuit in 1970.

English musician Sam Fender was at No.1 on the UK chart with his debut studio album Hypersonic Missiles. The album drew heavy comparisons to Bruce Springsteen due to Fender's "lyricism and his vignettes of working-class struggle."

American singer John ‘Bootsie’ Wilson from The Silhouettes died. The doo wop/R&B groups single 'Get A Job' was a No.1 hit on the Billboard R&B singles chart and pop singles chart in 1958. The doo-wop revival group Sha Na Na derived their name from the song's lyrics. 'Get A Job' is included in the soundtracks of the film American Graffiti, Trading Places and Stand By Me. The Silhouettes performed in the 1986 movie Joey.

Green Day released their seventh studio album American Idiot, their first album in four years. Overtly political in places, the album expresses the disillusionment and dissent of a generation that came of age in a period shaped by tumultuous events such as 9/11 and the Iraq War. With a more refined sound, the album outsells even their punk rock touchstone Dookie, released 10 years earlier.

Pink went to No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Just Like A Pill', the American singer's first UK No.1. The track, taken from her second studio album, Missundaztood peaked at No. 8 on the Billboard Hot 100 in the US.

The Fugees scored their second UK No.1 single with 'Ready Or Not'. The chorus in the song is based on 'Ready or Not Here I Come (Can't Hide from Love)' by The Delfonics. The Fugees previous single 'Killing Me Softly' was so successful that the track was 'deleted' and no longer supplied to retailers whilst the track was still in the Top 20 to make way for the next single 'Ready or Not'.

works.title: Don't Stand So Close To Me

description: With the help Of heavy MTV exposure, 'Money For Nothing' gave Dire Straits their first US No.1 single. The groundbreaking music video for the track was one of the first uses of computer-animated human characters. The song features a guest appearance by Sting, who sings the signature falsetto introduction, background vocals and a backing chorus of "I want my MTV" set to the same notes as the chorus of the Police's hit 'Don't Stand So Close To Me'.

Adam And The Ants were at No.1 on the UK singles chart with their second chart topper 'Prince Charming'. In 2010, an out-of-court settlement was reached, with a large sum of royalties received, after a musicologist found 'Prince Charming' to be musically identical to the 1965 Rolf Harris song 'War Canoe'.

works.title: You Took the Words Right Out of My Mouth
You Took the Words Right Out of My Mouth

description: Meat Loaf released his debut studio album Bat Out Of Hell. His first collaboration with composer Jim Steinman and producer Todd Rundgren, it is one of the best-selling albums of all time, having sold over 43 million copies worldwide (and still sells over 200,000 copies per year). The first single released from the album 'You Took the Words Right Out of My Mouth' failed to chart when first released.

Carl Douglas was at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Kung Fu Fighting.' The song was recorded in 10 minutes and had started out as a B-side. It went on to sell over 10 million and became one of the Best Selling Singles of all time.

works.title: Can't Get Enough Of Your Love Baby

description: Barry White went to No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Can't Get Enough Of Your Love Baby', the singers first and only US solo chart topper. It made No.8 in the UK.

Freda Payne was at No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Band Of Gold', the singer's only UK No. 1, and spent six weeks at the top of the chart. The song was written and composed by former Motown producers Holland–Dozier–Holland (under the pseudonym of Edythe Wayne) and Ron Dunbar. Motown session singers Pamela Vincent, Joyce Vincent Wilson, and Telma Hopkins provided the background vocals on the record. Wilson and Hopkins would later go on to form the group Tony Orlando & Dawn.

Country singer Jeannie C Riley went to No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Harper Valley PTA'. The single sold more than six million copies and marked the first time that a single by a woman topped both Billboard's Hot Country Singles chart and the Hot 100, a feat that would not be repeated until Dolly Parton's '9 to 5' 13 years later in 1981. Jeannie won a Grammy for the best female country singer of 68.

Deep Purple made No.4 on the US singles chart with their debut single 'Hush'. Written by American songwriter Joe South for singer Billy Joe Royal, the song was also a No. 14 hit by Somebody's Image (an Australian band fronted by Russell Morris) in 1967 and for Blue Swede in 1975, and by Kula Shaker in 1997.

American singer and actor Bobby Vinton started a three-week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Blue Velvet'. The single became a hit in the UK 27 years later when it reached No.2. As a teen idol, Vinton became known as "The Polish Prince", as his music paid tribute to his Polish heritage. Written and composed in 1950 by Bernie Wayne and Lee Morris, 'Blue Velvet' was a top 20 hit for Tony Bennett in its original 1951 version.
